records.name: Grid maze router (Lee, Hadlock, A*)

sources.title: An algorithm for path connections and its applications
A shortest path algorithm for grid graphs

records.mechanism: Lay a uniform grid over the free space, with a cell of one margin. Route each edge by A* over the free cells, with a cost for each bend and a cost (or a discount) for each cell that other routes use. Lee's wave is the breadth-first form. Hadlock orders the search by the number of detours.
records.math: Lee: breadth-first wave, path = grid distance. Hadlock: key d(P), length = manhattan(s,t) + 2 d(P). A*: f = g + h, h = manhattan, g = sum(len + beta * bend + gamma * used).
records.cost: O(G log G) per edge for G grid cells. 100 nodes: 1e4 to 1e5 cells, near 1 s for all edges. 1000 nodes: 1e6 cells, near 100 s without a coarse grid. CI only above 400 nodes.
records.screen: case-hub-chain, case-many-groups, small-clustered at cell = margin. Keep if R14 >= 0.95, R9 = 0, the R3 median <= corners + 1 and the time <= 10x corners at 100 nodes.

records.name: Line probe router (Hightower, Mikami-Tabuchi)

sources.title: A solution to line-routing problems on the continuous plane

records.mechanism: Shoot horizontal and vertical probe lines from both plugs. A probe stops at a box. Points on a probe start new probes at the next level. When a probe of the source meets a probe of the target, the way has few bends. The memory is the probes, not a grid.
records.math: Mikami-Tabuchi: level-k probes start from each point of the level k-1 probes. It finds a way when one exists, with the fewest bends among the probe levels. Hightower: one escape point per probe, fast, and it can fail.
records.cost: O(L n) per edge for L levels. 100 nodes: under 1 ms per edge. 1000 nodes: a few ms per edge.
records.screen: Same boards as EDA-001. Keep if the R3 median < corners, R6 <= 1.1x corners and no edge fails.

records.name: Hanan grid and orthogonal visibility graph router

sources.title: On Steiner's problem with rectilinear distance
Orthogonal connector routing
sources.authors: M. Wybrow, K. Marriott, P. J. Stuckey

records.mechanism: Build the orthogonal visibility graph: the lines through each box side and each plug, cut at the boxes. Route each edge by A* with a cost of length plus a penalty for each bend. Then nudge the parallel legs of different edges apart in each channel.
records.math: cost = L + beta * bends. The graph holds an optimal orthogonal route for this cost. Hanan: a rectilinear Steiner minimal tree exists on the Hanan grid.
records.cost: Build O(n log n + V), V up to O(n^2). Route O(V log V) per edge. 100 nodes: near 10 ms per edge. 1000 nodes: V near 1e5 to 1e6, slow without a sparse form.
records.screen: As EDA-001 against corners at 100 nodes. Keep if R3 <= corners, R14 = 1 and the time <= 5x corners.

records.name: Constrained left-edge tracks in each gap

sources.title: Wire routing by optimizing channel assignment within large apertures
Efficient algorithms for channel routing

records.mechanism: In each gap, give each link piece a track by the left-edge rule: sort by start, fill the lowest track first. Keep the order of two overlapping pieces only where a swap adds crossings. Two pieces that do not overlap share a track. Fewer tracks need less room.
records.math: Left edge: tracks = density d = max overlap, optimal for an interval graph with no constraint. With a constraint graph: tracks >= max(d, longest chain). Constraint i below j iff overlap(i, j) and cost(j, i) > cost(i, j).
records.cost: O(p^2) per gap for the constraint graph and O(p log p) per track. Under 5 ms at 100 nodes, near 100 ms at 1000 nodes.
records.screen: The scratch run of the note: lanes fall 5% to 26% at equal turn crossings. Keep if the sum of lanes falls >= 5% on 3 boards, R1 does not rise and M1 falls when roomDemand reads the track count.

result.note: The option `tracks: left-edge` of `gapLanes` is off by default. The sum of lanes falls 5% to 26% on 7 boards. Crossings stay the same or fall, except +0.1% on grid-400. R12 falls. M1 and M4 do not change, because `roomDemand` already reads the density. The screen has no room step, so the side table of the bench measured it.

strict.note: The screen field of the record decides on the lanes, R1 and M1 of the side table of the bench, not on the board count of B1 and the B3 q95. The screen artifacts have no raw values of that table. Thus the old verdict stays.

rescreen.note: The screen has no step `room`, so M1, M4 and R12 of `tracks: left-edge` have no new value.

records.name: Dogleg channel routing

sources.title: A dogleg channel router
Dogleg channel routing is NP-complete

records.mechanism: Let a long piece change its track inside a gap, at a place where another link turns (a dogleg). The split breaks long chains and cycles of the order constraints, so the gap needs fewer tracks.
records.math: Split each piece at the turn positions of the other pieces into sub-pieces. Assign the sub-pieces by the constrained left edge. Tracks >= density.
records.cost: As EDA-004 with up to two times the pieces.
records.screen: grid-400 and case-many-groups against EDA-004. Keep if the lanes fall >= 5% more and R3 rises <= 0.2 for each route.

records.name: Greedy channel router

sources.title: A greedy channel router
sources.authors: R. L. Rivest, C. M. Fiduccia

records.mechanism: Sweep each gap from one end to the other, column by column. At each column, bring the turning links to their side, join split tracks, and move tracks toward their next turn. It completes any gap and adds a track only where it must.
records.math: A column sweep with local rules. In practice the tracks are density + 0 to 2.
records.cost: O(columns x tracks) per gap.
records.screen: Against EDA-004 on its boards. Keep only if the lanes are >= 5% fewer at an R3 rise <= 0.2.

records.name: Switchbox routing at gap junctions

sources.title: A greedy switch-box router
Detour: a fast, accurate switchbox router
sources.authors: G. T. Hamachi, J. K. Ousterhout

records.mechanism: Treat each place where a row gap meets a column gap as a switchbox, with fixed lane ends on its four sides. Connect the lanes that turn there so that their order agrees with the tracks of both gaps. Lane crossings at junctions fall.
records.math: A channel with terminals on four sides. Greedy column sweep (Luk) or maze search (Detour). Objective: completion, then the fewest crossings of turning lanes.
records.cost: O(t^2) per junction for t lanes.
records.screen: case-many-groups and grid-400: lane crossings inside the junction rectangles. Keep if they fall >= 20% at an R3 rise <= 0.1.

records.name: Global routing on the gap graph, then tracks, then points

sources.title: Track assignment: a desirable intermediate step between global routing and detailed routing
sources.authors: S. Batterywala, N. Shenoy, W. Nicholls, H. Zhou

sources.title: NTHU-Route 2.0: a robust global router for modern designs
sources.authors: Y.-J. Chang, Y.-T. Lee, J.-R. Gao, P.-C. Wu, T.-C. Wang

records.mechanism: Make a coarse graph of the gaps and their junctions (the g-cells of a chip). Each g-cell has a capacity: its width over the lane spacing. First route each edge as a chain of g-cells, then give tracks in each gap (EDA-004), then make the points. Each stage sees the room.
records.math: Global: min sum_e cost(path_e) with sum usage(g) <= cap(g) as a soft limit. Tracks: constrained left edge per gap. Points: offsets of the track lines.
records.cost: O(n) g-cells. Global O(m G log G). 100 nodes: near 20 ms. 1000 nodes: near 1 s.
records.screen: packedGridBoard after openGaps, and case-many-groups. Keep if M4 = 0, R12 is better than shared and the R5 median stays within 5%.

records.name: Negotiated congestion (PathFinder)

sources.title: PathFinder: a negotiation-based performance-driven router for FPGAs

records.mechanism: Route all edges and let them overuse corridors, then repeat. Each pass raises the price of each overused corridor link, by its present overuse and by a history of past overuse. Edges with another good way leave. Stop when no corridor holds more lanes than its capacity.
records.math: c(a) = (b(a) + h(a)) * p(a). p(a) = 1 + pf * max(0, occ + 1 - cap). After each pass h(a) += hf * max(0, occ - cap), and pf grows by 1.3 to 2.
records.cost: 5 to 30 passes of the router. 100 nodes: 0.5 to 2 s. 1000 nodes: 20 to 60 s, CI only.
records.screen: case-dense-groups and packedGridBoard: count the overfull gaps (lanes > width / spacing). Keep if they fall >= 50% at an R5 median rise <= 5%.

records.name: Rip-up and reroute

sources.title: A simple yet effective technique for global wiring

records.mechanism: After one pass of `shared`, find the edges with a fault: through a box, out and back, or a bad lane crossing. Remove them and the edges in conflict with them. Route them again, with the other routes fixed, in a new order. A few rounds remove the effect of the first order.
records.math: Loop: F = edges with a fault. Unroute F and its neighbours, reroute by fault weight, and accept the round only when the total cost falls.
records.cost: Rounds x faulty edges. Near +30% time at 100 nodes and +50% at 1000 nodes.
records.screen: shared on case-hub-chain and case-many-groups with 5 seeds of the input order. Keep if the spread of R6 and R1 over the orders falls >= 50% and the medians do not rise.

records.name: Multicommodity flow with randomized rounding

sources.title: Randomized rounding: a technique for provably good algorithms and algorithmic proofs
Faster min-max resource sharing in theory and practice
sources.authors: D. Muller, K. Radke, J. Vygen

records.mechanism: Write the routing as a flow problem on the corner graph: each edge is a commodity, each link has a capacity. Solve the fractional problem, where an edge splits over several ways, with multiplicative weights. Then pick one way per edge at random by its fractional weight.
records.math: min lambda with sum_e x_e(a) <= lambda * cap(a). Resource sharing gives a (1 + eps) fractional optimum. Rounding gives a congestion of O(log G / log log G) times the optimum, with high probability.
records.cost: eps^-2 m log(links) shortest paths. eps = 0.1: near 100x the router. 100 nodes: near 10 s. 1000 nodes: CI only.
params: roundings: 1 to 20 seeds, keep the best
records.screen: tiny-uniform and the 3 case boards: the max overuse against EDA-009. Keep as a MEAS2 reference if its bound is within 20%. Keep as a router only if the time <= 10x shared at 100 nodes.

records.name: Lagrangian prices with a lower bound

sources.title: Archer: a history-based global routing algorithm
sources.authors: M. M. Ozdal, M. D. F. Wong

sources.title: The Lagrangian relaxation method for solving integer programming problems

records.mechanism: Give each capacity a price. Route each edge alone by its shortest way at the current prices, then raise each price by its overuse (a subgradient step). The routes approach a good solution, and the dual value is a lower bound on the best cost, so MEAS2 gets a gap to the optimum.
records.math: L(lambda) = sum_e min_p [len(p) + sum_{a in p} lambda_a] - sum_a lambda_a cap_a <= OPT. lambda_a <- max(0, lambda_a + t_k (use_a - cap_a)), t_k = theta (UB - L) / |g|^2.
records.cost: 20 to 200 iterations of m shortest paths. Like EDA-009.
records.screen: Boards of <= 30 nodes with an optimum from an ILP. Keep if the bound gap <= 15% and the routes are not worse than EDA-009.

records.name: Track assignment across gaps

sources.title: Track assignment: a desirable intermediate step between global routing and detailed routing
sources.authors: S. Batterywala, N. Shenoy, W. Nicholls, H. Zhou

records.mechanism: After the global ways, give each long piece a track in each gap, so that the pieces of one edge keep one track from gap to gap and lanes cross little at junctions. It is the lane order of ROOM-C, solved for all gaps together, not gap by gap.
records.math: Interval coloring per gap with cost w1 * overlaps + w2 * track changes + w3 * crossings. Greedy by length with local swaps, or an ILP on small boards.
records.cost: O(p log p) per gap for the greedy form. ILP on small boards only.
records.screen: case-many-groups and grid-400: B5 and R1 against gapLanes with the order crossings. Keep if crossings fall >= 15% at <= 5% more lanes.

records.name: Layer assignment as zoom levels

sources.title: Congestion-constrained layer assignment for via minimization in global routing

records.mechanism: Chips put long wires on high layers and count each layer change as a via. Treat each zoom level as a layer. Assign each edge the coarsest level where it shows alone, by its span and its group, with a budget for each level. A dynamic program on the tree of sections minimizes the changes of form along each route.
records.math: min sum_e vias(e) with items_d + links_d <= B_d. A via is a change from a level link to a route of its own. COLA solves one net on a tree exactly by dynamic programming.
records.cost: O(m x depth). Under 10 ms at 1000 nodes.
records.screen: nestedGridBoard and the levels of small-clustered. Keep if Z4 <= 1 at each level, Z9 is 10% better and Z1 = 0.

records.name: Rectilinear Steiner trunks (FLUTE)

sources.title: FLUTE: fast lookup table based rectilinear Steiner minimal tree algorithm for VLSI design
On Steiner minimal trees with rectilinear distance

records.mechanism: For a fan-out from one plug to k targets, replace the split point of `trunks` with a rectilinear Steiner tree of the plug and the targets. FLUTE looks up the optimal tree in a table for up to 9 points and splits larger nets. The trunk then uses the least ink for an orthogonal style.
records.math: RSMT on the Hanan grid. Hwang: RMST <= 1.5 RSMT. FLUTE is optimal up to degree 9. A euclidean form uses GeoSteiner on small sets.
records.cost: O(k log k) per net. Negligible against the router.
records.screen: trunks on mid-fanout and case-dense-groups: B1 and the total trunk length against the split of today. Keep if B1 rises >= 5% with R9 = 0 after an obstacle repair.

records.name: River routing for merges and buses

sources.title: An optimal solution to a wire-routing problem
Optimal placement for river routing
sources.authors: C. E. Leiserson, R. Y. Pinter

records.mechanism: Where a bundle of k lanes meets k plugs, or another bundle, in the same order, route the lanes as a river: in order, with no crossing, and with the lane spacing kept. Each lane takes the shortest way that keeps its distance from the lane before it.
records.math: Tompa: each wire hugs the previous one at distance s. The least separation of two rows comes in O(k). The routes are planar, so R1 = 0 inside the merge.
records.cost: O(k) per merge.
records.screen: shared-all on case-many-groups: R12 and B9 near the merges. Keep if the lane spacing errors fall >= 50% at no rise of R1.

records.name: Stretch balance in a bundle (inverse length matching)

sources.title: A length-matching routing algorithm for high-performance printed circuit boards
sources.authors: M. M. Ozdal, M. D. F. Wong

records.mechanism: Board routers make the wires of a bus equal in length. Here the goal is the inverse: choose where each lane leaves a bundle so that the stretch of the members stays even, and no member pays a large detour for the bundle. Prices on the members with too much stretch move their exits earlier.
records.math: min sum len with st(e) <= tau for each member. Lagrange: exit cost += lambda_e (st(e) - tau), and lambda_e grows with the excess.
records.cost: O(k x iterations) per bundle.
records.screen: trunks on mid-fanout. Keep if the B3 q95 falls >= 10% at a B1 loss <= 3%.

records.name: RUDY demand map for room

sources.title: Fast and accurate routing demand estimation for efficient routability-driven placement

records.mechanism: Before any route, spread each link as a uniform wire density over the bounding box of its two boxes. Sum the densities on a grid with prefix sums. The map tells which gaps need room before routing, so roomDemand can open them in one pass, and the host can see the hot spots.
records.math: d(x, y) = sum_e w (W_e + H_e) / (W_e H_e) for (x, y) in bbox(e). Use 2-D prefix sums. Gap demand = the integral of d over the gap.
records.cost: O(m + cells). Near 1 ms at 1000 nodes.
records.screen: The Spearman correlation of the RUDY demand and the demand of roomDemand with the method routes, on 5 boards. Keep if rho >= 0.8 at 10x less time.

records.name: Corner-stitched free tiles as the channel graph

sources.title: Corner stitching: a data-structuring technique for VLSI layout tools

records.mechanism: Split the free space into maximal horizontal rectangles (corner stitching). Each tile knows its neighbours and its width. Route on the tile graph, so each corridor has a known width and thus a capacity in lanes. The tiles also give the gaps for room without a sweep.
records.math: O(n) tiles. Point location in O(sqrt n) on average. capacity = floor(width / s).
records.cost: Build O(n log n). Route O(T log T) per edge for T tiles.
records.screen: The corridor capacities against boardGaps on the packed and nested boards. Keep as the base of EDA-008 if the build time <= the corner graph time.

records.name: Topological routing, then rubber bands

sources.title: SURF: rubber-band routing system for multichip modules
sources.authors: D. Staepelaere, J. Jue, T. Dayan, W. W.-M. Dai

sources.title: Computing minimum length paths of a given homotopy class
Algorithms for routing and testing routability of planar VLSI layouts
sources.authors: C. E. Leiserson, F. M. Maley

records.mechanism: First decide only the topology of each edge: on which side of each box it goes (its homotopy class). Then pull each edge tight like a rubber band, in its class, with a clearance around the box corners. The second stage gives the shortest way in that class and keeps the lanes of one class apart.
records.math: Homotopic shortest path by the funnel algorithm on a triangulation (Hershberger-Snoeyink). Routability: the capacity of each cut >= the flow across it (Leiserson-Maley).
records.cost: Triangulation O(n log n). O(n) per edge in the worst case. Near 1 s at 1000 nodes.
records.screen: corners against topology plus rubber band on the case boards. Keep if the R5 median falls >= 3% with a better R8 and no worse R1.

records.name: Fat-path bundle routing

sources.title: Drawing with fat edges
sources.authors: C. A. Duncan, A. Efrat, S. G. Kobourov, C. Wenk

sources.title: On the escape routing of differential pairs
sources.authors: T. Yan, P.-C. Wu, Q. Ma, M. D. F. Wong

records.mechanism: Route each bundle as one wide path of width k times the lane spacing, as a board router routes a differential pair as one trace. Grow the boxes by half that width and search the corner graph of the grown boxes. Then split the path into k lanes by offsets.
records.math: Configuration space: obstacles grown by w / 2, w = k s + clearance. A path in it has offsets at +-(i - (k - 1) / 2) s that are clear of the boxes.
records.cost: One corner graph for each width bucket (1, 2, 4, 8 lanes): <= 4 graphs, near 4x corners.
records.screen: shared-all on case-dense-groups and on packedGridBoard with no room step. Keep if M4 falls >= 80% at an R5 median rise <= 5%.

records.name: Ordered escape for plugs

sources.title: Ordered escape routing based on Boolean satisfiability
sources.authors: L. Luo, M. D. F. Wong

sources.title: Algorithmic studies on PCB routing (thesis)

records.mechanism: When many links leave one side of a box, order their plugs so that the stubs leave the box with no crossing and enter their bundles in lane order. A sort by the direction of the next leg gives the order. A min-cost flow gives each stub a free slot when slots are few.
records.math: Sort the plugs of one side by the angle of the first leg of each way. The stubs are then planar. Unordered escape: min-cost max-flow (optimal). Ordered escape: SAT (exact).
records.cost: O(k log k) per side. Flow O(k^2) on small sides.
records.screen: small-clustered and case-dense-groups: crossings within 2 u of a box. Keep if they fall >= 30%.

records.name: Push and shove for edits

sources.title: KiCad PCB editor: the interactive router

records.mechanism: When a host adds one edge, route it, and push the routes in its way aside to keep their clearance, instead of routing all edges again. A shove moves out to the next routes until each clearance holds or a limit stops it. The other routes keep their shape.
records.math: For each segment in collision: offset it by the clearance and pass the push on. On a failure, walk around.
records.cost: Local to the change. A few ms per edit.
records.screen: Add one edge to small-clustered, 20 times. Keep if the mean Frechet move (Z10) falls >= 80% against a full reroute, with R9 = 0.

records.name: Tangent arcs at any angle (TopoR style)

sources.title: TopoR topological router
SURF: rubber-band routing system for multichip modules
sources.authors: D. Staepelaere, J. Jue, T. Dayan, W. W.-M. Dai

records.mechanism: Draw each route as straight tangent lines and circle arcs around the corners that it passes, with the clearance as the radius. It is the shape of a rubber band around round pegs, with no grid of angles. The lanes of a bundle get concentric arcs.
records.math: A route is a chain of common tangents of circles of radius r = clearance + lane offset at the corners. It is G1, its length is exact, and its offsets are exact.
records.cost: O(points) per route.
records.screen: Against the curve arc on corners. Keep if the min R8 >= clearance on each route and C7 = 0 at a length rise <= 1%.

records.name: Octilinear grid router

sources.title: Metro maps on octilinear grid graphs
sources.authors: H. Bast, P. Brosi, S. Storandt

sources.title: The X architecture: not your father's diagonal wiring

records.mechanism: Lay an octilinear grid (8 directions) over the board. Route each edge by A* on the grid, with a cost for each bend by its angle and a lower cost on grid links that other edges of its bundle use. The style is the style of a metro map.
records.math: Grid graph with bend links inside each grid node, costs c135 < c90 < c45. A* per edge. The ILP form is exact for the grid.
records.cost: O(G log G) per edge. 100 nodes: near 1 s for all edges. 1000 nodes: CI only.
records.screen: The case boards: R2 mean angle and R3 against corners. Keep if R3 falls >= 20% at an R5 median rise <= 8%.

records.name: Exact lane order by ILP (metro-line crossing minimization)

sources.title: Efficient generation of geographically accurate transit maps
sources.authors: H. Bast, P. Brosi, S. Storandt

sources.title: Metro-line crossing minimization: hardness, approximations, and tractable cases
Edge routing with ordered bundles
sources.authors: S. Pupyrev, L. Nachmanson, S. Bereg, A. E. Holroyd

records.mechanism: Order the lanes of all runs together by an integer program. Each pair of edges on each run has one variable. A crossing costs where their order changes from run to run, and a separation costs where two edges part and meet again. Rules on the graph first fix most pairs, so the program stays small.
records.math: x_ab^r in {0, 1} (a left of b on run r). A crossing at a junction when x^r != x^r'. min sum w_c crossings + w_s separations. MLCM is NP-hard. MLCM-P has an O(sqrt(log L)) approximation.
records.cost: An ILP. Seconds at 100 nodes after the rules. Needs a solver in wasm (HiGHS or GLPK).
records.screen: shared-all on case-many-groups and small-clustered: lane crossings against laneOrder bundle. Keep as a MEAS2 reference in any case. Keep as a strategy if B5 falls >= 10% within 2 s at 100 nodes.

records.name: Route schematization (C-oriented paths)

sources.title: Schematization of networks
sources.authors: S. Cabello, M. de Berg, M. van Kreveld

sources.title: Path schematization for route sketches
sources.authors: D. Delling, A. Gemsa, M. Nollenburg, T. Pajor

records.mechanism: Turn each route into a path that uses only a set of directions (4, 6 or 8), with the fewest legs and near the route. A dynamic program over the points of the route gives it. A test keeps it clear of the boxes and keeps its side of the other routes.
records.math: min legs with Frechet <= delta and the topology kept. Dynamic program O(k^2) per route for a fixed set of directions.
records.cost: O(k^2) per route. Some ms in total.
records.screen: On the routes of corners. Keep if R3 falls >= 30% with R9 = 0 and C8 max <= 2 u.

records.name: Weber hubs

sources.title: A quadratic integer program for the location of interacting hub facilities
Weiszfeld's method: old and new results

records.mechanism: The router `sections` puts each hub at the center of its section. Put it at the weighted geometric median of the plugs of the edges that use it, as a hub-location model places a hub. Weiszfeld steps find that point. Ways through the hub get shorter and turn back less.
records.math: h* = argmin sum_i w_i |h - p_i|. Weiszfeld: h <- (sum w_i p_i / |h - p_i|) / (sum w_i / |h - p_i|). p-hub median with the inter-hub discount alpha (O'Kelly).
records.cost: O(edges through the hub x 20 steps). Negligible.
records.screen: sections and sections-tree on case-hub-chain and small-clustered, and mid-clustered in CI. Keep if the R5 median falls >= 3% and R7 does not rise.

records.name: Branched transport cost (Gilbert flow cost)

sources.title: Minimum cost communication networks
Optimal paths related to transport problems

records.mechanism: Give each shared link the cost len * f^alpha, with f the number of edges on it and 0 < alpha < 1. Edges together cost less than apart, so ways merge where the saving pays for the detour. alpha = 1 gives no bundles. The discount of shared is a fixed form of it.
records.math: E = sum_links len(a) f(a)^alpha. The marginal cost of one more edge on a link with f edges is len ((f + 1)^alpha - f^alpha). Route in order with that cost, then reroute each edge with the others fixed.
records.cost: As shared x 1 to 5 passes.
records.screen: shared-all with alpha 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 1 on case-many-groups and small-clustered: the front of B1 against the B3 q95. Keep if one setting is better than discount 0.5 on both.

result.note: The option `cost: flow` of `shared` is off by default. No alpha from 0.5 to 0.8 beats `discount` 0.5 on B1 and the B3 q95 on more than 1 of the 4 boards. A smaller alpha gives more B1 and fewer crossings, but a longer stretch. For example, `shared-all` alpha 0.5 on small-clustered: B1 0.430 to 0.558, R1 305 to 209, B3 q95 1.359 to 2.218. An alpha of 0.8 gives the inverse. The only win is many-groups with `shared` (B1 0.083 to 0.085, q95 1.000 both). hub-chain does not change. The group stays screened, because its rider HWY-039 (the rip-up) is a win.

strict.note: With the strict rule, shared-flow-a05 against shared wins 1 of 4 boards (2 with the old rule). The verdict does not change.

rescreen.note: `shared-flow-a06` is at least as good as `shared` on each new win on `dense-groups`, `hub-chain`, `many-groups`. It is better on `dense-groups`, `many-groups` and equal on `hub-chain`. `shared-all-flow-a07` is at least as good as `shared-all` on each new win on `small-clustered`, `dense-groups`, `hub-chain`, `many-groups`. It is better on `small-clustered`, `dense-groups`, `hub-chain`, `many-groups`. The option `shared-all-flow-a07` closes a median of 0 of the gap, with the rule `collection`. The gap closed uses only the 3 boards `tiny-uniform` of 10 nodes. It is a hint, not a verdict.

activation.note: 8 of 8 candidates are exercised on a decision board. The verdict does not change.

records.name: Gilbert split point for trunks

sources.title: Minimum cost communication networks

records.mechanism: The router `trunks` puts its split at a fixed share (0.5) of the way to the center of the targets. Put the split where the flow cost len * f^alpha of the trunk and its branches is least. There, the branches meet the trunk at Gilbert's angles, which depend on their counts.
records.math: min over s: len(p, s) k^alpha + sum_j len(s, t_j) f_j^alpha, by weighted Weiszfeld steps. Angle of two branches m1, m2: cos(theta) = ((m1 + m2)^(2 alpha) - m1^(2 alpha) - m2^(2 alpha)) / (2 m1^alpha m2^alpha). Equal flows: alpha 0.5 gives 90 degrees, alpha 0 gives 120 degrees.
records.cost: O(k x iterations) per trunk. Negligible.

records.name: Kernel density estimation edge bundling (KDEEB) with an obstacle mask

records.math: on(e) = min{s : dist(first(e)(s), spine) <= w}, off(e) = max{s : ...}. Clamp so that on < off and the ramp turn <= theta_max.
records.cost: O(p log p) per edge with a grid on the spine. 100 nodes: < 5 ms. 1000 nodes: < 30 ms.
params: rule: meet, Steiner angle, fixed share
records.screen: Use the clusters of corridor signatures on 3 boards. Keep if B6 and B3 q95 drop at a B1 loss < 3%.

records.name: Width, lanes and capacity: split a highway that does not fit

sources.title: The physiological principle of minimum work: I. The vascular system and the cost of blood volume

records.mechanism: The width of a highway is its lanes times the lane gap, capped by maxWidth. Where a gap between boxes is narrower than the width, the highway splits into two parallel highways in two gaps. Or it asks the room step for space. A width rule f^beta gives a calmer far view, with beta near 1/3 as in Murray's law.
records.math: W = min(maxWidth, n w) for lanes, or W = w0 n^beta for one fat line. If W > gap(l) on a link l: split the lanes into two sets by lane order, or add demand W - gap(l) to the room step.
records.cost: O(links of the spine) per highway.
params: on narrow gap: split, room or squeeze
records.screen: Boards: packedGridBoard, case-dense-groups. Keep if M4 reaches 0 at an M1 rise < 10% or a B1 loss < 10%.

records.name: Highways for each zoom level that nest

records.mechanism: Each zoom level gets its own set of highways from the same rule with a coarser scale. A highway of a fine level must lie inside one highway of the coarser level. Thus zooming in only splits highways and does not move them. Far levels show few wide highways. Close levels show many narrow ones.
records.math: Scale sigma_d = sigma_0 r^d. H_d = rule(edges, sigma_d) restricted to the edges of each h in H_{d-1}. Nesting check: each h in H_d has its edges inside one h' in H_{d-1}.

records.name: Scale space with persistence

sources.title: Topological persistence and simplification

records.mechanism: Run a density or clustering rule at many scales. Track each highway from the scale where it is born to the scale where it merges into a larger one. Long-lived highways are real, short-lived ones are noise. The zoom levels take the highways that live at their scale, so a zoom shows only stable structure.
records.math: persistence(h) = log(sigma_death / sigma_birth). Keep h at level d if sigma_d in [sigma_birth, sigma_death) and persistence(h) >= p0.
records.cost: S scales times the rule. 100 nodes: 50 to 200 ms. 1000 nodes: 0.5 to 2 s.

records.name: Stable highway ids across edits

records.mechanism: After an edit, the rule starts from the previous highways (warm start). Each new highway gets the id of the old highway with the most common edges. A renderer can then animate a highway as one object. Unmatched highways are new, and their old ones end.
records.math: Match by max sum J(h, h') with the Hungarian method, J = Jaccard of the edge sets, keep matches with J >= 0.5. Warm start: seed the clusterer with the old centroids.
records.cost: O(H^3) Hungarian, or greedy O(H log H). 1000 nodes: < 10 ms greedy.
records.screen: The seeded edits of Z10 on the 5 screen boards. Keep if Z10 mean and moved share drop by 20%.

records.name: Local growth by accretion and extension
records.mechanism: Start with the longest edge as a seed highway. Each next edge, from long to short, joins the highway that gives it the largest saving, if the saving beats its own route. A highway extends at an end while enough lanes go on together. The growth is local, fast and online.
records.math: save(e,h) = len(first e) - (ramp_in + t spine part + ramp_out). Join argmax_h save if > 0, else e is a new seed. Extend an end while >= k lanes stay within w of each other.
records.cost: O(m H) with a grid on the spines. 100 nodes: < 10 ms. 1000 nodes: 30 to 100 ms.
records.screen: Screen boards: case-dense-groups, case-hub-chain, case-many-groups, small-clustered (5 seeds) and mid-fanout (1 seed). Baselines: corners, shared, trunks. Keep if B1 >= 0.9 x shared at 1/3 of its time on 3 of 5 boards.

records.name: Level links become highways
records.mechanism: At the far view, a level link stands for the edges between two items. At the close view, those same edges ride one highway along the path of that level link. The highway set is thus the level links, and a zoom shows the same lines that open into lanes.
records.math: For each level link (A, B, count) with count >= minSize: highway spine = link points outside A and B, edges = the edges from A to B. Ramps through the corner graph inside A and B.
records.cost: O(m) after the levels. 100 nodes: < 5 ms. 1000 nodes: < 20 ms.
records.screen: Boards: case-many-groups, nestedGridBoard, mid-clustered. Keep if Z9 drops by 50% with R7 <= sections.

records.name: Gap highways
records.mechanism: The room step knows the gaps between boxes and the demand of each gap. A gap with demand of k or more lanes holds one highway along its middle line. The highways of neighbour gaps join at the crossings of the gaps. The highway network is thus the street plan of the board.
records.math: Gap graph: nodes = gap crossings, links = gap middle lines. Demand from the first routes. Highway link if demand >= k. Edges route on the gap graph with the highway discount.
records.cost: O(gaps + m log gaps). 100 nodes: < 10 ms. 1000 nodes: 30 to 80 ms.
params: gap source: room step or the corner graph
records.screen: Boards: packedGridBoard, grid-400, nestedGridBoard. Keep if B1 >= shared and M4 = 0 on 2 of 3 boards.

result.note: The records are the screen-v2 run 40761862381 and the screen-v1 run 40764832307, at a32522f. On both sets, gaps is better on B1 and on R14 with 0 families against. records.name: Orthogonal streets by set cover

sources.title: A greedy heuristic for the set-covering problem
Drawing and labeling high-quality metro maps by mixed-integer programming

records.mechanism: For an orthogonal style, candidate streets are horizontal and vertical lines in the gaps. Each street covers the edges whose legs can run on it with a small detour. A greedy set cover picks the few streets that cover the most edges. Edges then route with legs on the streets.
records.math: Candidates: gap lines y = c, x = c. cover(street) = {e : detour of e via street <= s}. Greedy: pick the street with the largest new cover per unit length, until the gain < g0.
records.cost: O(C m) for C candidates. 100 nodes: < 20 ms. 1000 nodes: 0.1 to 0.3 s.
records.screen: Boards: grid-400, packedGridBoard. Keep if R14 > 0.9 and B1 >= shared at B3 q95 <= 1.3.

records.name: Local search over the highway set on the measures

sources.title: Optimization by simulated annealing

records.mechanism: Start from any highway set. Moves add a candidate, drop a highway, move one edge to another highway, or move a merge point. Each move is kept if a weighted sum of the measures improves, or by an annealing rule. The search tunes the result on the measures of MEAS0 directly.
records.math: Score = w1 B1 - w3 B3_q95 - w4 B4 - w6 B6. Accept if delta > 0 or with probability exp(delta / T). T falls by 0.95 per sweep.
records.cost: Sweeps times moves times the delta cost. 100 nodes: 0.1 to 0.5 s. 1000 nodes: 2 to 10 s, so CI only.
params: moves: add, drop, move edge, move point
records.screen: Boards: the 3 case boards. Keep if it gains 5% on the score over its start set. It also gives an upper bound for the fast rules.

records.name: Interchanges: a network of highways

sources.title: Spatial generalization and aggregation of massive movement data

records.mechanism: Highways do not stay alone: they meet at interchanges, where edges change from one highway to another. An edge can ride two or three highways in a row. The interchanges sit where several highways come near, and a budget limits their count. The highways thus make a small road graph of the board.
records.math: Interchange candidates: points where >= 2 spines come within w. Each edge takes the cheapest path over the highway graph with a change cost c. Keep interchanges with >= k changes.
records.cost: O(H^2 + m H log H). 100 nodes: < 20 ms. 1000 nodes: 0.1 to 0.4 s.
records.screen: Screen boards: case-dense-groups, case-hub-chain, case-many-groups, small-clustered (5 seeds) and mid-fanout (1 seed). Baselines: corners, shared, trunks. Keep if B1 > the best single-highway rule by 5% at B3 q95 within 5% on 3 of 5 boards.

records.name: Physarum highways

sources.title: Rules for biologically inspired adaptive network design
sources.authors: Tero, Takagi, Saigusa, Ito, Bebber, Fricker, Yumiki, Kobayashi, Nakagaki

sources.title: A mathematical model for adaptive transport network in path finding by true slime mold
Physarum can compute shortest paths
IRLS and slime mold: equivalence and convergence

records.mechanism: Run the slime-mold tube model on the corner graph with the edge ends as food sources. Tubes with flow thicken, the rest thin out. The thick tubes are the highways. Each edge then takes the cheapest way with link cost L / D^beta.
records.math: Q_ij = D_ij (p_i - p_j) / L_ij; sum_j Q_ij = +I0 at the source, -I0 at the sink, 0 elsewhere; dD_ij/dt = f(|Q_ij|) - D_ij with f(q) = q^g / (1 + q^g). Large g or small I0 gives a tree near the MST or Steiner tree; small g or large I0 keeps loops.
records.cost: O(T k E sqrt(V)) for T steps and k Laplacian solves (conjugate gradient) per step. 100 nodes (about 400 corners, 3 000 links, T 150, k 6): 0.3 to 1 s. 1000 nodes: 5 to 20 s on the corner graph, CI only, or under 0.5 s on the hub graph of the sections.
params: keep threshold on D 0.01 to 0.2, default 0.05
records.screen: Boards case-many-groups, small-clustered and mid-fanout (one seed, 100-node cut for mid-fanout). Against shared-all: keep if B1 >= shared-all + 0.05 and B3 q95 <= shared-all + 0.10 on 2 of 3 boards, with 0 rule violations.

records.name: Physarum agents on a field

sources.title: Characteristics of pattern formation and evolution in approximations of Physarum transport networks

records.mechanism: Many particles with three forward sensors walk on a grid. Each turns toward the strongest trail, steps, and drops trail. The trail spreads and fades. Nodes emit attractant. The trail network between the nodes, thinned to a skeleton, gives the shared ways of the far view.
records.math: Sensors at angles -SA, 0, +SA and distance SO; rotate by RA toward the largest sensed value; move SS; deposit dep; trail T <- decay * mean3x3(T). Typical SA 22.5 or 45 degrees, RA 45 degrees, SO 9 cells.
records.cost: O(T (A + G)) for T steps, A agents and G cells. A 256 x 256 grid with 10 000 agents and 300 steps: 0.3 to 1 s, nearly independent of n. Skeleton extraction O(G).
records.screen: Level links of case-dense-groups at the far view. Keep only if Z3 faults are 0 and B1 of the level links rises by 0.10 over levelLinks. Expected to drop: a raster model ignores exact boxes.

records.name: Loops from changing loads

sources.title: Damage and fluctuations induce loops in optimal transport networks
Fluctuations and redundancy in optimal transport networks

records.mechanism: Leaf veins form loops because the load moves around. Adapt the conductances to several load cases at once (one per collection or per source group). Loops survive where two heavy loads want different ways, so routes get alternatives and the worst detour drops.
records.math: Minimize the mean dissipation <sum_e Q_e^2 / C_e> over load cases with sum_e C_e^gamma = K. Fixed point: C_e proportional to <Q_e^2>^(1/(1+gamma)), then rescale to the budget K. gamma < 1 gives loops that grow with the spread of the loads.
records.cost: Per iteration one Laplacian solve per load case, 20 to 60 iterations. 100 nodes: under 0.5 s. 1000 nodes: 2 to 10 s, CI only, or run on the hub graph.
params: budget K as a share of the full graph 0.05 to 0.5
records.screen: mid-hubs and case-hub-chain. Against NAT-001 at the same kept length: keep if R6 drops by 10% or more and B1 falls by 0.03 or less.

records.name: Canalization feeder trees to hubs

sources.title: A model for vein formation in higher plants
The control of the patterned differentiation of vascular tissues
Self-organization of the vascular system in plant leaves: inter-dependent dynamics of auxin flux and carrier proteins

records.mechanism: In a leaf, every cell makes auxin and the stalk drains it. Channels that carry flux get more conductive, so the flow gathers into veins. In each section, make each member node a source and the hub the sink. The routes to the hub merge into one feeder tree.
records.math: phi_ij = D_ij (c_i - c_j) / L_ij; sum_j phi_ij = s_i with s_i = 1 for each member and -(members) at the hub; dD_ij/dt = |phi_ij|^mu - r D_ij, mu > 1 gives a tree. One solve per step, as NAT-001 with many sources and one sink.
records.cost: One small solve per step per section. 100 nodes: about 50 ms. 1000 nodes: 0.5 to 1 s.
records.screen: Router sections on mid-clustered (100-node and 1000-node seeds) and case-hub-chain. Keep if B1 rises by 0.05 or more over today's sections, with R7 not worse.

records.name: Active walker trails

sources.title: Modelling the evolution of human trail systems
Active walker model for the formation of human and animal trail systems

records.mechanism: Route all edges in passes. Each route leaves footprints that make the ground more comfortable, and comfort fades back. In the next pass a link costs less near comfortable ground. Routes gather on shared trails, between a direct way system and a minimal way system.
records.math: dG/dt = (G0 - G) / T + I (1 - G / Gmax) sum_a delta(r - r_a); V_tr(r) = integral exp(-|r - r'| / sigma) G(r') d2r'; heading e_a = (d_a - r_a + grad V_tr) / norm. kappa = I T / sigma^2: small kappa gives direct ways, large kappa a minimal way system.
records.cost: P passes times the time of the router shared, plus a blur of the comfort grid per pass. P = 4: about 4 times shared. 100 nodes: about 0.4 s. 1000 nodes: a few seconds, CI only.
records.screen: Against shared-all on case-many-groups, small-clustered and mid-fanout: the front of B1 against R5 q95, and Z10 after one seeded added edge. Keep if it dominates shared-all on one board and is not dominated on the others.

result.note: NAT-005 is screened with HWY-005, as the option `reuse` of the router `shared`. The baseline is `shared-all`. With 2 passes and `reuse: 1`, B1 rises on each board (0.430 to 0.624 on small-clustered), and crossings fall 23% to 89%. But the q95 rises on each board (1.359 to 2.475 on small-clustered), so neither dominates the other.

strict.note: With the strict rule, shared-p2 against shared wins 0 of 4 boards (2 with the old rule). The verdict does not change.

rescreen.note: `shared-all-wind-p2-r1` is at least as good as `shared-all` on each new win on `small-clustered`, `dense-groups`, `hub-chain`, `many-groups`. It is better on `small-clustered`, `dense-groups`, `hub-chain`, `many-groups`. The gap closed uses only the 3 boards `tiny-uniform` of 10 nodes. It is a hint, not a verdict.

records.name: Desire-line room

sources.title: Modelling the evolution of human trail systems

records.mechanism: People cut across a lawn where the paved way makes a long detour. Draw each edge as its straight desire line, weight it by the detour of its first route, and count the weight that crosses each gap. Open the gaps that the desire lines want, so the routes go straighter.
records.math: demand(g) = sum_e w_e [the straight line of e crosses gap g or the box next to it], w_e = delta_e - 1 from a first routing (or 1). Feed demand to openGaps in place of the lane count, under an area budget.
records.cost: O(m times gaps crossed) with the bucket grid, plus one routing pass. 100 nodes: under 10 ms plus the route. 1000 nodes: about 50 ms plus the route.
records.screen: packedGridBoard and nestedGridBoard. Against roomDemand at the same M1: keep if R5 q95 is 5% lower or better.

records.name: Ant colony router

sources.title: Ant system: optimization by a colony of cooperating agents
Ant colony system: a cooperative learning approach to the traveling salesman problem
MAX-MIN ant system
Structure and formation of ant transportation networks
sources.authors: Latty, Ramsch, Ito, Nakagaki, Sumpter, Middendorf, Beekman

records.mechanism: Ants of each collection walk the corner graph from source to target. They pick links by pheromone and length. Short tours drop more pheromone, and pheromone evaporates. With one pheromone per collection, the ants of a collection meet on common ways.
records.math: p_ij = tau_ij^alpha eta_ij^beta / sum_l tau_il^alpha eta_il^beta, eta_ij = 1 / L_ij; tau <- (1 - rho) tau + sum_k Q / L_k; MAX-MIN clamps tau to [tau_min, tau_max]. Final route: the greedy argmax path of tau^alpha eta^beta.
records.cost: O(I m a len deg) for I iterations, a ants per edge, path length len and degree deg. 100 nodes (I 30, a 4): about 0.1 s. 1000 nodes: about 2 s.
records.screen: Against shared on case-many-groups, small-clustered and mid-fanout, 5 seeds. Keep if B1 >= shared + 0.03 with R5 q95 not worse. Expected to tie with shared at a higher cost.

records.name: Expected ants

sources.title: Ant system: optimization by a colony of cooperating agents

records.mechanism: Replace the sampled ants by their expected visits. The ant walk from a source is a Markov chain with an absorbing target. One linear solve gives the expected visits of each link. The pheromone update uses these values, so the result needs no seed.
records.math: P = row-normalized tau^alpha eta^beta, with eta_ij = exp(k cos(angle to target)) / L_ij; visits n solve (I - P_T^T) n = e_source on the transient part; flow_ij = n_i P_ij; tau <- (1 - rho) tau + c flow.
records.cost: Per iteration one sparse solve per source group, as one step of NAT-001. 100 nodes: 0.1 to 0.3 s. 1000 nodes: 2 to 5 s, CI only.
records.screen: Against NAT-007 and NAT-001 on the same 3 boards. Keep if B1 is within 0.02 of the better of the two at a lower time, with no seed spread.

records.name: Two-way lanes

sources.title: Self-organized lane formation and optimized traffic flow in army ants
Social force model for pedestrian dynamics

records.mechanism: On army-ant trails, outbound ants take the outer lanes and returning ants the middle lane. Walkers in a counterflow form lanes by direction. In each run, sort the lanes by direction first (keep right), then by the bundle order, so edges that go one way stay side by side.
records.math: Lane key = (direction class relative to the run, then the bundle order). Keep right: lanes along the run direction on its right side. Variant outer: two outer lanes for one direction, the middle for the other.
records.cost: O(sum over runs of k log k). Negligible at 100 and 1000 nodes.
params: weight against the bundle order 0 to 1, default 1
records.screen: shared-all on case-many-groups and mid-fanout with directed edges. Keep as a style option if end crossings are within +2% of laneOrder bundle. Keep as a default only if they drop.

records.name: Termite hubs

sources.title: A model for the emergence of pillars, walls and royal chambers in termite nests
sources.authors: Bonabeau, Theraulaz, Deneubourg, Franks, Rafelsberger, Joly, Blanco

sources.title: A brief history of stigmergy

records.mechanism: Termites drop material where the scent of fresh material is strong, so deposits grow into evenly spaced pillars. Let each straight edge line drop material on a grid. The scent spreads and fades, the peaks grow and space out. Put the hubs of the sections at the peaks.
records.math: dP/dt = Phi - k1 P + D_P lap(P) - g div(P grad H); dC/dt = k1 P - k2 C; dH/dt = k2 C - k4 H + D_H lap(H). Simplified: C <- C + k C blur(C) - decay C, then local maxima with suppression radius r.
records.cost: O(T G) plus O(m len) to drop the material. A 128 x 128 grid and 50 steps: under 50 ms at 100 and 1000 nodes.
records.screen: sections with hubs at the peaks against today's hubs on mid-hubs and case-hub-chain. Keep if R5 q95 drops by 5% with R7 not worse.

records.name: Optimal channel networks

sources.title: Minimum energy and fractal structures of drainage networks
sources.authors: Rinaldo, Rodriguez-Iturbe, Rigon, Bras, Ijjasz-Vasquez, Marani

sources.title: Fractal river basins: chance and self-organization
Generation and application of river network analogues for use in ecology and evolution

records.mechanism: River basins form the spanning tree that makes the total energy small, with a cost that grows slower than the flow. For the edges of one fan, find the tree on the corner graph that makes the sum of flow^gamma times length small. Heavy flows merge into trunks.
records.math: E = sum_i k_i Q_i^gamma L_i with gamma = 0.5; Q_i = edges whose path uses link i. Local move: change the downstream link of one vertex; accept if E drops (or by annealing). Start from the shortest-path tree.
records.cost: Sweeps S times V times degree times depth. 100 nodes (400 corners, S 20): under 50 ms per fan. 1000 nodes: about the time of trunks times 2.
params: annealing T0 0 (greedy) to 1, with a seed
records.screen: trunks against this tree on mid-fanout and small-clustered. Keep if its (B1, B3 q95) point is on the front against the trunks rule at each split.

records.name: Branched transport junctions

sources.title: Minimum cost communication networks
Optimal paths related to transport problems
Optimal transportation networks: models and theory

records.mechanism: The cost of a way grows with its load as w^alpha with alpha below 1, so sharing pays. For each fan, merge targets into Y junctions where the weighted pulls of the three branches balance. alpha 1 gives straight edges, alpha 0 a Steiner tree. The junction angle follows the load.
records.math: cost = sum_e w_e^alpha L_e. At a Y: w0^alpha e0 + w1^alpha e1 + w2^alpha e2 = 0 (unit vectors out of the junction), so cos(theta1) = (w0^(2 alpha) + w1^(2 alpha) - w2^(2 alpha)) / (2 w0^alpha w1^alpha). Equal split: cos(theta/2) = 2^(alpha - 1): 120, 90 and 74.9 degrees at alpha 0, 0.5 and 2/3. Junction point by weighted Weiszfeld steps.
records.cost: O(k^2) per fan for the merge order plus O(k iterations) for the junctions. Under 10 ms at 100 nodes, under 100 ms at 1000 nodes, plus A* repair of branches that hit a box.
records.screen: trunks with these junctions against split on mid-fanout and small-clustered. Keep if B6 max <= 60 degrees and B1 >= trunks, with 0 rule violations after the repair.

records.name: Murray widths and angles

sources.title: The physiological principle of minimum work: I. The vascular system and the cost of blood volume
Optimality principles in arterial branching
On connecting large vessels to small: the meaning of Murray's law

records.mechanism: Vessels keep the cube of the radius constant over a split. Give each closed bundle and each level link a drawn width that grows as count^(1/3), not as the count. Thick bundles stay narrow, merges look continuous, and the gaps need less room. Use the matching junction angle.
records.math: r0^3 = sum_i r_i^3, so width = w0 k^(1/3). Minimum-volume angle: cos(theta1) = (r0^4 + r1^4 - r2^4) / (2 r0^2 r1^2). With r^3 proportional to the flow, this is NAT-012 with alpha = 2/3.
records.cost: O(segments). Negligible.
records.screen: shared-all on case-many-groups: room demand with widths k^(1/3) against lane widths k. Keep if M1 drops by 5% or more with M4 = 0.

records.name: Vascular tree by constrained construction

sources.title: Computer-optimization of vascular trees
A three-dimensional model for arterial tree representation, generated by constrained constructive optimization

records.mechanism: Grow the tree of a fan one target at a time. Join each new target to the existing segment where a new split adds the least total volume, with radii from Murray's law. Then scale the radii of the whole tree again.
records.math: Volume V = pi sum_i r_i^2 L_i; resistance R = 8 eta L / (pi r^4); flows fixed by the targets; r from Murray's law with exponent 3. For each candidate segment, place the split point by weighted Weiszfeld steps and keep the least dV.
records.cost: O(k^2) candidates per fan, O(k^3) worst case with rescaling. k up to 50: a few ms per fan at 100 and 1000 nodes.
records.screen: Same boards as NAT-012. Keep if B1 is higher than NAT-012 at an equal B3 q95. Otherwise merge it into NAT-012 as its construction order.

records.name: Space colonization trunks

sources.title: Modeling and visualization of leaf venation patterns
sources.authors: Runions, Fuhrer, Lane, Federl, Rolland-Lagan, Prusinkiewicz

sources.title: Modeling trees with a space colonization algorithm

records.mechanism: The targets of a fan are attractors. From the source plug the tree grows in steps. Each attractor pulls its nearest tree node. Each pulled node grows a new node along the mean direction to its attractors. An attractor dies when a node comes within the kill distance.
records.math: n_v = sum over s in S(v) of (s - v) / |s - v|; v' = v + D n_v / |n_v|; remove s when |s - v| < d_k; S(v) holds the attractors within d_i whose nearest node is v.
records.cost: O(steps (S + V) log) with the bucket grid. A fan needs span / D steps. Under 10 ms at 100 nodes, under 100 ms at 1000 nodes.
records.screen: mid-fanout and small-clustered against trunks. Keep if B1 rises by 0.05 with B3 q95 within +0.10 and 0 rule violations.

records.name: Closed venation backbone for levels

sources.title: Modeling and visualization of leaf venation patterns
sources.authors: Runions, Fuhrer, Lane, Federl, Rolland-Lagan, Prusinkiewicz

sources.title: The relative neighbourhood graph of a finite planar set

records.mechanism: In closed venation, a vein grows to a source from each node in its relative neighbourhood, which makes loops. At a zoom level, link the items by their relative neighbourhood graph and route each level link along it, so the far view shows a calm network with a few loops.
records.math: Relative neighbourhood graph: p-q is a link if no r has max(d(p, r), d(q, r)) < d(p, q). Each level link takes the cheapest way on that graph with cost L (1 - discount if shared).
records.cost: O(k log k) through the Delaunay graph, or O(k^2) for k items. Under 10 ms for up to 1000 items.
records.screen: Level links of case-dense-groups and case-many-groups. Keep if the level faults (Z3) are not worse and the ink of the level drops by 10%.

records.name: Balancing-factor trees

sources.title: One rule to grow them all: a general theory of neuronal branching and its practical application

records.mechanism: Dendrites follow one rule: grow a minimum spanning tree where each new point joins the tree at the place that makes its wire length plus bf times its path length to the root least. bf 0 gives the least wire, a large bf gives direct paths. One knob trades ink against detour.
records.math: Greedy (Prim with a changed cost): add t* = argmin over t not in T, v in T of d(t, v) + bf PL(v), with PL(v) the path length from the root to v. Joining at segments (not only nodes) adds Steiner points.
records.cost: O(k^2) per fan, or O(k) A* searches with corner-graph distances. Under 10 ms at 100 nodes, under 100 ms at 1000 nodes.
records.screen: Sweep bf over 0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.7 and 1 on mid-fanout and small-clustered. Keep if one bf dominates the default point of trunks on (B1, B3 q95).

result.note: The option `fan: tree` of `trunks` is off by default. bf 0.2 and 0.4 beat `trunks` on B1 and the B3 q95 on dense-groups (B1 0.081 to 0.095 with bf 0.2). On small-clustered, the q95 falls but B1 falls 4%. hub-chain and many-groups do not change. A smaller bf gives more B1, so a screen of bf 0 and 0.1 is next.

strict.note: With the strict rule, trunks-tree-bf02 against trunks wins 1 of 4 boards (3 with the old rule). The verdict does not change.

rescreen.note: The option `trunks-tree-bf04` closes a median of 0.071 of the gap, with the rule `collection`. The gap closed uses only the 3 boards `tiny-uniform` of 10 nodes. It is a hint, not a verdict.

records.name: Knee of the plant Pareto front

sources.title: High-resolution laser scanning reveals plant architectures that reflect universal network design principles

records.mechanism: Plant shoots sit on the Pareto front of total length against the path length to the root, at a place that depends on their conditions. Compute the front of each fan by a sweep of the weight, and give each fan its own knee point, not one global knob.
records.math: cost_a(T) = a L(T) + (1 - a) sum_t PL(t); front by a in {0, 0.1, ..., 1} with the greedy tree of NAT-017; knee = the point farthest from the chord of the normalized front.
records.cost: 11 times NAT-017. Under 0.1 s at 100 nodes, under 1 s at 1000 nodes.
records.screen: Against NAT-017 with its best fixed bf: keep if the hypervolume of (B1, B3) is higher on 2 of 3 boards.

records.name: Bronchial space-filling splits

sources.title: A three-dimensional model of the human airway tree
An optimal bronchial tree may be dangerous

records.mechanism: The airway tree splits its region in two, gives each child the flow of its half, and points each child toward the center of its half. For a trunk, split the targets in two by a line through the tip, branch toward the center of each half, and repeat until one target is left.
records.math: Flow ratio r = Q1 / Q0. Child direction: toward the centroid of its subset. Angles from r with Murray's exponent: cos(theta1) = (1 + r^(4/3) - (1 - r)^(4/3)) / (2 r^(2/3)). Branch length: a share of the distance to the centroid.
records.cost: O(k log^2 k) per fan. Under 10 ms at 100 and 1000 nodes.
params: split: count | weight | widest angle gap
records.screen: Same boards as NAT-017. Keep if not dominated by the best bf of NAT-017 on (B1, B3 q95) and B6 is lower.

records.name: Mycelial spanner backbone

sources.title: Biological solutions to transport network design
On sparse spanners of weighted graphs
Rules for biologically inspired adaptive network design

records.mechanism: Fungi build a cheap tree and then fuse hyphae to add loops where transport is slow. Build a minimum spanning tree over the hubs as the backbone. Add a shortcut between two hubs when the backbone way is more than t times their direct distance and much traffic goes between them.
records.math: Greedy t-spanner over the hubs: for pairs in order of decreasing demand (ties by distance), add (u, v) if d_B(u, v) > t d(u, v) and w_uv >= w_min. Report the measures of Tero 2010: length over MST, mean distance over MST, and the fault tolerance.
records.cost: O(h^2 log h) for h hubs. h is about n / 8: under 1 ms at 100 nodes, about 10 ms at 1000 nodes.
records.screen: sections on case-hub-chain and mid-hubs. Keep if R6 drops by 10% with B1 lower by 0.02 at most.

records.name: Tropism growth router

sources.title: A dynamic root system growth model based on L-Systems
A fast marching level set method for monotonically advancing fronts

records.mechanism: A root tip grows in steps and turns toward a cue with a limited turn rate, and away from stones. Grow each route from its plug along the normal. Turn toward the falling geodesic distance to the target, at most a set angle per step, and away from near boxes. The path has bounded curvature.
records.math: h_(k+1) = normalize(h_k + s_t grad(phi_target) + s_o grad(phi_obstacle)), turn per step <= dtheta_max, step length s. phi_target is the geodesic distance field (no local minima). Curvature <= dtheta_max / s.
records.cost: One distance field per target, cached: O(G log G) each. 100 nodes with a 128 x 128 grid: 0.3 to 1 s. 1000 nodes: CI only, or guide by the A* path of corners in place of a field.
params: max turn 5 to 45 degrees per step, default 15
records.screen: case-many-groups and small-clustered against corners with the clothoid curve. Keep if C3 median is lower, R5 q95 is within +5% and no rule fails.

records.name: Axon zipper

sources.title: Axon tension regulates fasciculation/defasciculation through the control of axon shaft zippering
Models of axon guidance and bundling during development
A model of fasciculation and sorting in mixed populations of axons

records.mechanism: Axons that touch at a small angle zip together: adhesion pulls them into one bundle and tension resists. After any router, find pairs of legs that run near and almost parallel. Zip them onto one shared line when the shared length gain beats the cost of extra length and turn.
records.math: Zip if a overlap - tension dL > 0, with angle <= theta_max and distance <= d_max. Zipped line: length-weighted mean of the two legs. Our reading of the zipper vertex balance: cos(theta/2) = 1 - Gamma / (2 T), adhesion Gamma, tension T.
records.cost: O(S log S) for the pairs with the bucket grid, a few passes. About 5 ms at 100 nodes, 50 to 100 ms at 1000 nodes.
params: adhesion ratio Gamma / T 0 to 1, default 0.3
records.screen: A post step on corners and on plugs routes, case-dense-groups and small-clustered. Keep if B1 rises by 0.05, B4 rises by 0.03 at most and R9 stays 0.

result.note: The strategy `zipper` beats `shared` on 2 of the 4 boards, and `adhesion: 1` also on 2. It fails only on the q95, by 0.1% to 1.5%. Against `shared-ways`, B1 rises 12% to 199% on all 4 boards, B2 rises, and R1 falls on 3 boards. B6 and R4 rise. The screen has no measure of B7 or R12. A stretch gate can make it pass. The strategy stays in the registry.

strict.note: With the strict rule, zipper-a1 against shared wins 3 of 4 boards (2 with the old rule): small-clustered, dense-groups and hub-chain. On hub-chain, the q95 rises 1.000 to 1.001, a tie. But on hub-chain, B4 rises from 0.063 to 0.316 and R1 from 68 to 80, and the screen field of the record forbids that rise. Thus the guard keeps the record dropped. Strict count 3, kept dropped by the guard.

rescreen.note: `zipper` is at least as good as `shared` on each new win on `small-clustered`, `dense-groups`, `hub-chain`. It is better on `small-clustered`, `dense-groups`, `hub-chain`. The gap closed uses only the 3 boards `tiny-uniform` of 10 nodes. It is a hint, not a verdict.

activation.note: 6 of 6 candidates are exercised on a decision board. The verdict does not change.

records.name: Harmonic field router

sources.title: Path planning using Laplace's equation
Real-time obstacle avoidance for manipulators and mobile robots
Mathematical guidance for axons

records.mechanism: Growth cones climb an attractant from the target and turn from repellents. Solve Laplace's equation in the free space with the target low and the boxes as walls, then follow the gradient. A harmonic field has no local minimum, so each route arrives. With a source and a sink, the routes are electric field lines.
records.math: lap(phi) = 0 in the free space; phi = 0 on the target; boxes Dirichlet (phi = 1) or Neumann (d phi / dn = 0, insulating). Route: dx/ds = -grad(phi) / |grad(phi)|. Dipole: +1 at the source, -1 at the target.
records.cost: One solve per target: O(G iterations) by SOR or multigrid. A 128 x 128 grid and 200 iterations: 3 million updates per target. 100 nodes: 0.3 to 1 s. 1000 nodes: CI only, or only for the level links.
records.screen: Level links of case-dense-groups and case-many-groups. Keep if Z3 faults are 0 and R8 rises by 20% over levelLinks.

records.name: Pioneer and follower order

sources.title: Models of axon guidance and bundling during development

records.mechanism: Pioneer axons grow first and later axons follow them. In the routers with shared ways, the order of the edges decides which ways become shared. Route the pioneers first: the edges with the longest span, or with the most edges between their two sections. The followers then get the discount.
records.math: Order key = -span(e), or -load(e) with load the number of edges between the same two sections, ties by edge id. Then the router shared runs as today.
records.cost: O(m log m) on top of shared. No change in time class.
records.screen: shared-all with the 4 orders on 5 boards, 5 seeds each. Keep an order if A12 >= 0.64 on B1 against the input order, with R5 q95 not worse.

result.note: The default order `span` (the longest first) is the pioneer order. The base is `order: input`. With `shared-all`, B1 rises 6.2% and 5.3% on small-clustered and dense-groups, and R1 falls 19% and 10%. With `shared`, B1 rises 6.2% on dense-groups and R1 falls 0.7%. On many-groups with `shared-all`, R1 rises 7%. The order `load` does not beat `span`.

strict.note: The screen field of the record decides on B1 against the order input, not on the board count of B1 and the B3 q95. With the strict rule, B1 of the order span is better on 3 of 4 boards and worse on many-groups (0.718 against 0.722). The verdict does not change.

activation.note: 2 of 2 candidates are exercised on a decision board. The verdict does not change.

records.name: Soap-film Steiner trees

sources.title: How to find Steiner minimal trees in Euclidean d-space
A new class of Steiner tree heuristics with good performance: the iterated 1-Steiner approach
Obstacle-avoiding Euclidean Steiner trees in the plane: an exact algorithm

records.mechanism: A soap film between pins makes the shortest network, with three ways at 120 degrees at each junction. For each fan or collection with three ends or more, build a Steiner tree that avoids the boxes, and route the edges along it. It is the upper bound of ink saving.
records.math: Minimize sum L. Steiner points have degree 3 and angles of 120 degrees. Iterated 1-Steiner: add the candidate point that cuts the MST length most, repeat. Rectilinear: candidates on the Hanan grid.
records.cost: Iterated 1-Steiner: O(k^3 log k) per fan, k up to 30: a few ms. Exact methods only for small fans. Plus A* repair near boxes.
records.screen: mid-fanout and small-clustered: B1 against NAT-012 at alpha 0. Keep as the reference bound of B1 in the bench, not as a default.

records.name: Elastic band curves

sources.title: Elastic bands: connecting path planning and control
The heat equation shrinking convex plane curves

records.mechanism: A soap film in two dimensions is a shortest line, and a rubber band tightens until it touches its pegs. Treat each route as an elastic band. Tension shortens and smooths it, and a soft push from the boxes keeps clearance. Run a fixed number of steps.
records.math: x_i <- x_i + k_c (x_(i-1) + x_(i+1) - 2 x_i) + k_r sum_b grad(rho_b(x_i)), rho_b = max(0, d0 - dist(x, b)). Curve-shortening flow: dx/dt = kappa N.
records.cost: O(P iterations) with the bucket grid. About 10 ms at 100 nodes, about 100 ms at 1000 nodes.
records.screen: The curve step on corners routes, case-many-groups and small-clustered. Keep if C3 median drops by 20% against smooth, with the counts curve-clear and curve-ends at 0.

records.name: Crystal metric

sources.title: Geometric models of crystal growth
Zur Frage der Geschwindigkeit des Wachsthums und der Auflosung der Krystallflachen

records.mechanism: Crystals grow fastest along preferred directions, so they take polygon shapes. Route under a metric whose unit ball is a polygon: a square for an orthogonal style, an octagon for an octilinear style, a circle for free style. Routes then use few directions and few bends.
records.math: ||v||_W = min { lambda : v in lambda W } for the Wulff shape W, plus a bend cost b per turn. Shortest path on a state graph of (corner, direction).
records.cost: A* on the corner graph times 4 or 8 directions: 4 to 8 times corners. 100 nodes: about 0.2 s. 1000 nodes: 2 to 5 s.
records.screen: corners with the octagon against corners on small-clustered and grid-400. Keep if R3 drops by 20% with R5 q95 within +5%.

records.name: Lightning growth

sources.title: Fractal dimension of dielectric breakdown
Diffusion-limited aggregation, a kinetic critical phenomenon
Fast animation of lightning using an adaptive mesh

records.mechanism: Lightning and diffusion-limited aggregation grow a branched channel in a Laplacian field. The growth chance of each frontier cell is the field there to the power eta. eta 1 is aggregation, a large eta gives straight channels. A channel grown from a source toward its targets is a branched trunk.
records.math: lap(phi) = 0, phi = 0 on the channel, phi = 1 at the targets; p_i = |grad(phi_i)|^eta / sum_j |grad(phi_j)|^eta. Deterministic limit: grow at the argmax.
records.cost: One Laplace solve per growth step: 1 000 steps on 10 000 cells with 50 iterations is 500 million updates, seconds per fan. CI only.
records.screen: One fan of mid-fanout at 100 nodes. Keep only if B1 >= NAT-015 and R4 <= NAT-015. Expected to drop.

records.name: Crack partition

sources.title: Hierarchical crack pattern as formed by successive domain divisions
Four sided domains in hierarchical space dividing patterns

records.mechanism: Drying mud cracks in order. Each new crack splits one domain across its long side and meets the older cracks at right angles, so the domains nest. Split each section by a crack that follows the gaps between the boxes, not a straight line, and pick the crack that cuts the fewest edges.
records.math: Crack = cheapest path across the cell on the gap graph (the dual of the free space), cost = edges cut + lambda length; across the longer side; ends at the older crack (T junction). Balance limit beta as the rule cut.
records.cost: One shortest path on the gap graph per split. 100 nodes: a few ms. 1000 nodes: about 50 ms.
params: most turns of a crack 0 to 8
records.screen: Against cut on the 10 boards of GRP-R at the same k. Keep if G2 at the far view is lower on 6 of 10 and G5 is not worse.

records.name: Erosion of a cost field

sources.title: A detachment-limited model of drainage basin evolution
The synthesis and rendering of eroded fractal terrains

records.mechanism: Water carves valleys where flow gathers, and slopes creep smooth. Route all edges on a cost grid, count the routes per cell as the flow, lower the cost there, smooth the field, and route again. Channels form, and the smoothing sets their spacing.
records.math: dz/dt = U - K A^m S^n + D lap(z), with z the cost field, A the route count per cell and S the local slope. A larger D / K gives wider spacing between channels.
records.cost: P passes of grid A* for m edges plus a blur. 100 nodes, 128 x 128 grid: about 0.1 s per pass. 1000 nodes: CI only.
records.screen: Against NAT-005 on the same boards. Keep if not dominated on (B1, R5 q95). Otherwise make it an option of NAT-005.

records.name: Ripple spacing of plugs

sources.title: Eolian dunes: computer simulations and attractor interpretation
A theoretical model for aeolian impact ripples

records.mechanism: Sand ripples settle at an even spacing through a short-range push. On each side of a box, treat the plugs as beads: each is pulled toward the place that faces its other end and pushed from its neighbours. Keep the order of the targets. The exact answer is an isotonic fit with a gap.
records.math: Minimize sum_i (x_i - t_i)^2 subject to x_(i+1) - x_i >= s and the side limits, with the plugs in the order of their target angles. Substitute y_i = x_i - i s and run pool-adjacent-violators: exact, O(k).
records.cost: O(k log k) per side for the sort. Negligible at 100 and 1000 nodes.
records.screen: small-clustered and mid-hubs. Keep if R11 q05 rises by 0.2 with R1 not worse. Fixed plugs do not move.

result.note: This rider of WILD-002 is the option `plugGap: 8`. The R11 q05 rises by more than 0.2, but R1 grows 3% to 5% on dense-groups and small-clustered.

strict.note: The screen field of the record decides on R11 and R1 of the router corners, not on the board count of B1 and the B3 q95. R1 grows 3% to 5% on 2 boards, a loss above the minimum effect. The verdict does not change.

rescreen.note: The gap closed uses only the 3 boards `tiny-uniform` of 10 nodes. It is a hint, not a verdict.

activation.note: 1 of 1 candidates are exercised on a decision board. The verdict does not change.

records.name: Phyllotaxis plug slots

sources.title: A better way to construct the sunflower head

records.mechanism: Sunflower seeds sit at golden-angle steps, so each new seed lands in the largest gap and no seed moves. Give the plug slots of a hub or a round item golden-angle steps, or golden-ratio steps along a side. A new edge adds one slot and moves no other plug.
records.math: theta_k = k 137.508 degrees; along a side, x_k = frac(k / phi) times the side length (a Weyl sequence). The ratio of the smallest to the largest gap stays above 1 / phi. Edges take slots by sorted angle.
records.cost: O(k log k) per side. Negligible.
records.screen: small-clustered and case-hub-chain, one seeded added edge. Keep if the moved share of Z10 drops by 30% with R11 q05 >= 0.35.

records.name: Foam groups

sources.title: Least squares quantization in PCM
Capacity-constrained point distributions: a variant of Lloyd's method
The physics of foams

records.mechanism: A dry foam relaxes to cells of equal area with walls that meet at 120 degrees. Start with k seeds, give each node to a seed with a capacity, move each seed to the center of its nodes, and repeat. Groups get equal sizes and round shapes. Repeat inside each group for the next level.
records.math: Capacity-constrained Voronoi: swap pairs of nodes between two groups when the swap lowers sum |c_v - s_g|^2 and keeps |g| = n / k. Lloyd step: s_g <- mean of c_v in g. Optional edge term alpha cut(g).
records.cost: O(t n log n) with the swaps. Under 10 ms at 1000 nodes for k 4 to 16.
records.screen: Against kd on the 10 boards of GRP-R at the same k. Keep if G4 rises by 0.05 and G5 is not worse.

records.name: Grassfire corridors

sources.title: A transformation for extracting new descriptors of shape
Voronoi diagrams: a survey of a fundamental geometric data structure

records.mechanism: A grass fire lit at all box edges burns inward. The fronts meet on the medial axis, the line farthest from all boxes. Use the medial axis of the free space as the road graph. Highways then run down the middle of the gaps with the most clearance, and short spurs join the plugs.
records.math: Medial axis = the Voronoi diagram of the box sides (or a grid distance transform and its ridges). Link cost L (1 + lambda / clearance). Spurs: the shortest clear segment from a plug to the axis.
records.cost: O(n log n) for the segment Voronoi diagram, or O(G) on a grid. About 50 ms at 1000 nodes, then routing as shared.
records.screen: shared-all on the axis graph against shared-all on the corner graph, small-clustered and case-dense-groups. Keep if tight drops by 50% with R5 q95 within +10%.

records.name: Snell merges

sources.title: Fermat's principle of least time (refraction, Snell's law)

records.mechanism: Light bends where it enters a faster medium. If a highway costs d < 1 per unit, the cheapest way to join it arrives at the angle acos(d) to the highway, not at a right angle. Put each merge and exit point where the route meets the highway at that angle.
records.math: Minimize sqrt(h^2 + x^2) + d (X - x): the optimum has cos(theta) = d. The merge point lies h d / sqrt(1 - d^2) before the foot of the perpendicular. Scratch check: d 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 give 75.5, 60.0, 41.4 degrees.
records.cost: O(1) per merge and exit. Negligible.
params: discount d 0.3 to 0.9 (the discount of shared)
fallback: perpendicular when the line is not clear
records.screen: shared and trunks on case-many-groups and mid-fanout. Needs B6 in the suite. Keep if B6 max <= 75 degrees and R9 stays 0.

result.note: The option `merge: snell` of `shared` is off by default. The B6 max falls on each board with merges: 8% to 27%. The ink rises 0.5% at most. The crossings rise 6% to 13% (18 to 24 on hub-chain), because the new merge lines cut across other routes. The option is only in `shared`, not in `trunks`.

strict.candidate: shared-all-snell against shared-all, on the B6 max
strict.note: The screen field of the record decides on the B6 max, not on the board count of B1 and the B3 q95. With the strict rule, the B6 max of shared-all-snell is better on 4 of 4 boards. With shared, it is better on 2 and a tie on 2. The verdict does not change.

rescreen.note: The option `shared-all-snell` closes a median of -0.004 of the gap, with the rule `all`. The gap closed uses only the 3 boards `tiny-uniform` of 10 nodes. It is a hint, not a verdict.
