records.name: Magnetic flow direction

sources.title: Graph drawing by the magnetic spring model

records.mechanism: In the magnetic spring model, edges act as compass needles that turn to a field: parallel, radial or round. Add a cost to each leg that points against a chosen field. All routes then flow one way, for example left to right or out from the center, and fewer routes go back.
records.math: Sugiyama and Misue: torque proportional to c_m b |d|^a theta^b. Here, leg cost = L (1 + c_m ((1 - cos theta) / 2)^beta), theta the angle between the leg and the field at its midpoint.
records.cost: The time of corners or shared plus O(1) per link. No change in time class.
records.screen: mid-fanout with a parallel field along the flow. Keep if R7 drops by 30% with R5 q95 within +5% against corners.

records.name: Current corridors

sources.title: A measure of betweenness centrality based on random walks
Centrality measures based on current flow
Graph sparsification by effective resistances

records.mechanism: Put one unit of current in at each source and take it out at its target. The current spreads over all ways, more on the short ones. Add the absolute currents of all edges on each link of the corner graph. Links with a high total are the corridors for highways. The other edges route alone.
records.math: L p = b_e for each edge (or each source group); I_link = sum_e |c_ij (p_i - p_j)|; a corridor is a link with I >= the q quantile. Then shared with the discount on corridor links. Faster: a seeded sketch with O(log m) random +1/-1 right sides.
records.cost: One Laplacian solve per source group. 100 nodes: about 0.1 s. 1000 nodes: 1 to 3 s, or under 0.5 s with a sketch of 16 solves.
records.screen: Against shared-all on case-many-groups, small-clustered and mid-fanout. Keep if not dominated on (B1, B3 q95) and B4 is lower.

records.name: Boids lanes

sources.title: Flocks, herds and schools: a distributed behavioral model
Novel type of phase transition in a system of self-driven particles

records.mechanism: Sample each route into points. Each point steers by three rules among the near points of other routes with a similar direction: align with them, move toward them, and keep a minimum distance. Bundles form with lanes at the separation distance, not on one line.
records.math: dx_i = w_a (mean u_j - u_i) + w_c (mean x_j - x_i) + w_s sum (x_i - x_j) / |x_i - x_j|^2 over |x_i - x_j| < s; neighbours within r with cos(direction) >= c; a spring to the first route and a push from the boxes.
records.cost: O(iterations P neighbours). 100 nodes (4 000 points, 30 iterations): a few ms. 1000 nodes: about 0.3 s.
records.screen: A post step on corners routes, small-clustered and case-dense-groups. Keep if B7 drops by 10% with R9 at 0.

records.name: Cell-sorting groups

sources.title: Reconstruction of tissues by dissociated cells
Simulation of biological cell sorting using a two-dimensional extended Potts model

records.mechanism: Mixed cells sort out because like cells stick more strongly. Give each node a group label. On the graph of neighbours on the board, a label pays an adhesion cost for each neighbour with another label and gains for each edge kept inside. A size term keeps groups near the target size.
records.math: H = sum over neighbour pairs of J (1 - delta(s_i, s_j)) - sum over edges of w delta(s_i, s_j) + lambda sum_g (a_g - A)^2. Zero-temperature sweeps: each node takes the neighbour label with the least H.
records.cost: O(sweeps (n kappa + m)): about 5 ms per sweep at 1000 nodes, 20 sweeps.
records.screen: Against cut on the 10 boards of GRP-R at the same k. Keep if G2 at the far view is lower on 6 of 10 with G5 not worse.

records.name: Reaction-diffusion hub spacing

sources.title: The chemical basis of morphogenesis
A theory of biological pattern formation

records.mechanism: An activator that excites itself and a fast inhibitor make spots at an even spacing. Seed the activator with the node density on a coarse grid and run it. The spots are the hub places, spaced by the range of the inhibitor. Nodes join the nearest spot. A larger range gives the next level.
records.math: da/dt = rho a^2 / h - mu_a a + D_a lap(a) + rho_0 s(x); dh/dt = rho a^2 - mu_h h + D_h lap(h). The spacing grows with sqrt(D_h / D_a).
records.cost: O(T G): a 128 x 128 grid and 2 000 steps, 0.1 to 0.3 s, nearly independent of n.
records.screen: Hubs from the spots against the hubs of the quadtree in sections. Keep if the spread of log(Z5) drops by 30% with G2 worse by 0.03 at most.

records.name: Meinhardt nets

sources.title: Morphogenesis of lines and nets

records.mechanism: Meinhardt showed that an activator and inhibitor with a substrate that the new cells use up make net lines that branch toward the places in need, like veins. Make the edge ends the places in need. The line cells that remain are a highway net.
records.math: da/dt = c s a^2 / h - mu a + D_a lap(a) + rho_0 y; dh/dt = c s a^2 - nu h + D_h lap(h); ds/dt = c_0 - gamma s - eps y s + D_s lap(s); dy/dt = d a - e y + y^2 / (1 + f y^2). y marks the line cells and does not go back.
records.cost: O(T G) with 4 fields: a 256 x 256 grid and 5 000 steps is more than 1 billion updates, seconds. CI only.
records.screen: small-clustered at the far view only. Drop unless B1 >= NAT-001 at a lower time. Expected to drop.

records.name: Remodelling room

sources.title: Adaptive bone-remodeling theory applied to prosthetic-design analysis
sources.authors: Huiskes, Weinans, Grootenboer, Dalstra, Fudala, Slooff

records.mechanism: Bone adds mass where the load is high and removes it where the load is low. Give the gaps a fixed extra area. In each pass, a gap grows by its lane load over its width and shrinks where the load is low. Then route again.
records.math: Stimulus S_g = lanes_g laneWidth / w_g; w_g <- w_g (1 + eta (S_g / S* - 1)); rescale so that sum w_g = budget. Huiskes: d rho / dt = B (S / rho - k).
records.cost: P passes of route plus roomDemand. 100 nodes with P = 3: about 0.3 s. 1000 nodes: a few seconds.
records.screen: packedGridBoard: M4 at M1 1.25 against roomDemand with maxGrowth 0.25 (ROOM-A: 2 lane routes through a box at 1.46). Keep if M4 is 0 at M1 1.35 or less.

records.name: Annealing of the discrete choices

sources.title: Optimization by simulated annealing
Drawing graphs nicely using simulated annealing

records.mechanism: Cooling metal finds a low-energy state because it accepts some worse moves while it is hot. Search the discrete choices that the greedy steps fix: the side of each free plug, the lane order of each run and which edges join a bundle. The energy is a weighted sum of the MEAS0 scores.
records.math: Accept a move with probability min(1, exp(-dE / T)); T_(k+1) = c T_k; E = sum_i w_i score_i, each score scaled as in the method of MEAS0.
records.cost: Moves times the time of dE. Lane orders only (local crossings): about 0.1 s for 10 000 moves. With a reroute per move: seconds to minutes, CI only.
records.screen: Lane order only, shared-all on case-many-groups. Keep if end crossings drop by 10% against laneOrder bundle.

records.name: Evolution of the options (NSGA-II)

sources.title: Adaptation in natural and artificial systems
A fast and elitist multiobjective genetic algorithm: NSGA-II

records.mechanism: A population of option settings evolves by crossover and mutation. Sorting by Pareto rank and crowding keeps a spread-out front of the measures. It gives TUNE a front over many options at once, not one sweep per option.
records.math: Fast non-dominated sort O(M N^2), crowding distance, binary tournament, simulated binary crossover and polynomial mutation.
records.cost: Generations times population times one route: 50 x 40 x 0.1 s = 200 s at 100 nodes. CI only.
records.screen: Two options of shared (discount, margin) against the grid sweep of OPTS. Keep if the front has the same hypervolume within 2% with fewer runs.

records.name: MAP-Elites atlas of settings

sources.title: Illuminating search spaces by mapping elites

records.mechanism: Quality-diversity search keeps the best setting in each cell of a grid of looks, for example ink saved against detour. The result is an atlas of distinct good settings. The playground shows it, so a reader picks a look and not a weight.
records.math: Archive A[cell(b(x))] keeps argmax f. Loop: pick an elite with a seeded draw, mutate it, evaluate it, and insert it if it beats the elite of its cell.
records.cost: As NAT-044: CI only for a full atlas. A precomputed atlas per example board is a static file.
params: descriptors: B1 x R5 | B2 x C3
records.screen: shared with the highway curve on one board. Keep if the archive fills 30% more cells than a grid sweep with the same number of runs.

records.name: Particle swarm and CMA-ES tuning

sources.title: Particle swarm optimization
Completely derandomized self-adaptation in evolution strategies

records.mechanism: Particles fly through the space of options, pulled to their own best and to the best of the swarm. CMA-ES moves and shapes a Gaussian cloud. Both tune the continuous options for one weighted score with few runs.
records.math: PSO: v <- w v + c1 r1 (p - x) + c2 r2 (g - x); x <- x + v. CMA-ES: sample N(m, sigma^2 C), then update m, C and sigma from the ranks.
records.cost: 20 particles x 30 iterations x one route. CI only above 100 nodes.
records.screen: Two options of shared against the grid sweep. Keep if it reaches 1% of the best grid score with a third of the runs or fewer.

records.name: Firefly and bee searches

sources.title: Firefly algorithms for multimodal optimization
A powerful and efficient algorithm for numerical function optimization: artificial bee colony (ABC) algorithm
The bees algorithm
sources.authors: Pham, Ghanbarzadeh, Koc, Otri, Rahim, Zaidi

sources.title: Metaheuristics: the metaphor exposed

records.mechanism: Fireflies move toward brighter ones with an attraction that fades with distance, so the swarm splits over several peaks. A bee colony sends more bees to rich sites and scouts to new ones. Both find several distinct good settings. They are close cousins of particle swarms.
records.math: Firefly: x_i <- x_i + beta0 exp(-gamma r_ij^2) (x_j - x_i) + alpha (rand - 0.5). ABC: v_ij = x_ij + phi (x_ij - x_kj), phi in [-1, 1]; onlookers pick i with p_i = fit_i / sum fit; a scout replaces a site after limit failures.
records.cost: As NAT-046.
records.screen: As NAT-046. Keep only if it finds a second distinct optimum that NAT-046 misses (hypervolume +5%). Expected to drop.

records.name: Use-it-or-lose-it pruning

sources.title: Decreasing-rate pruning optimizes the construction of efficient and robust distributed networks

records.mechanism: The brain makes too many synapses and then prunes the ones that carry little traffic, at a rate that falls with time. Start from all the runs of shared-all. Prune the runs that save the least, at a falling rate, and route the edges of a pruned run alone.
records.math: Prune share p_t = p0 r^t; usage u = (edges of the run - 1) times its length; remove the lowest u first. Navlakha and others: a falling rate gives more efficient and robust networks than a constant or a rising rate.
records.cost: Rounds times the reroute of the affected edges: 2 to 3 times shared-all.
records.screen: shared-all on case-many-groups and mid-fanout. Keep if B4 drops by 0.05 with B1 lower by 0.03 at most.

records.name: Multiscale Physarum across levels

sources.title: Rules for biologically inspired adaptive network design

records.mechanism: Run the tube model on the coarse level first, on the items and their links. Use its tubes as the starting conductance of the next finer level. The highways of the fine level then follow the level links of the far view, so a zoom keeps the map.
records.math: D^(d+1)_0(link) = 1 + kappa D^(d)(the corridor of its parent items), then NAT-001 at level d+1 with fewer steps.
records.cost: The sum over the levels, with fewer steps at the fine levels: about half of NAT-001.
records.screen: nestedGridBoard and case-dense-groups against NAT-001 alone. Needs Z9 in the suite. Keep if Z9 drops by 30%.

records.name: Elastic band: springs along the route and a push from the boxes

sources.title: Elastic bands: connecting path planning and control
Real-time obstacle avoidance for manipulators and mobile robots

records.mechanism: The base router gives a route. The route becomes a chain of points with a spring between each pair of neighbors. Each point gets a push away from the boxes from the distance field. The chain relaxes for a fixed number of steps. The ends stay on their plugs.
records.cost: O(I·V) for I steps and V route points. 100 nodes: 5 ms. 1000 nodes: 60 ms.
records.screen: On `case-dense-groups` and `mid-clustered`, after `corner`: keep it if the median R8 rises by 30% with R9 = 0 and R1 up by 5% or less.
records.rules: Short routes, smooth routes, a clearance d0 from each box.
records.hardRules: project. The push grows near a box, and a projection step moves each point with φ < d0 out along ∇φ. The plug ends are fixed.
records.zoom: warm and anchor. Each level starts from the route of its parent level.

records.name: Rule-energy edge bundling with a box field

sources.title: Force-directed edge bundling for graph visualization
Real-time obstacle avoidance for manipulators and mobile robots

records.mechanism: Force-directed edge bundling pulls the points of compatible edges together. This variant adds the box distance field as a second force and a hard projection. A stretch budget limits the pull on each edge. So bundles form only in free space, not through a box.
records.math: F_i = k_s Δx_i + Σ_{q ∈ C(e)} c(e,q) (x_{q,i} - x_i) / ‖x_{q,i} - x_i‖ + k_b ∇φ(x_i), stop the pull when length(e) > s_max · length0(e)
records.cost: O(C·m·P·I) for C candidate partners, P points per edge and I steps. 100 nodes: 40 ms. 1000 nodes: 1.5 s with a grid of neighbors.
params: points per edge 1 to 64 (doubles each cycle)
records.screen: On `mid-clustered` and `case-dense-groups`, against `trunks`: keep it if B1 is equal or better, B4 rises by 10% or less, and R9 = 0.
records.rules: Ink, bundles, clearance from boxes, a stretch budget for each edge.
records.hardRules: project after each cycle, then RULE-046.
records.zoom: warm and anchor. The compatibility uses the level links of each level.

result.note: The strategy `fdeb` beats `shared` on 0 of the 4 boards, alone and with the gate `stretch`. The paired median ratios are 0.68 for B1 and 0.96 for the q95. B7 rises on each board, so the bundles do not use less area. B2 rises on each board, but B1 falls on 3 boards. The option `pullLimit` replaces the option `budget` of the record, because the gate `stretch` has an option `budget`.

strict.note: With the strict rule, fdeb against shared wins 0 of 4 boards (0 with the old rule). The verdict does not change.

activation.note: 4 of 4 candidates are exercised on a decision board. The verdict does not change.

records.name: Route-to-route repulsion with a cutoff

sources.title: Graph drawing by force-directed placement
Efficient, high-quality force-directed graph drawing

records.mechanism: Each route point carries a like charge. Points of other routes push it away inside a cutoff radius. The push spreads parallel routes into lanes and opens narrow crossing angles. Edges of one bundle do not push each other, so the bundles stay.
records.math: F_i = Σ_{j ∉ e, ‖x_i - x_j‖ < r_c} q² (x_i - x_j) / ‖x_i - x_j‖³, neighbors from a grid hash
records.cost: O(I·V·k) for k neighbors in the cutoff. 100 nodes: 8 ms. 1000 nodes: 120 ms.
records.screen: On `mid-hubs` and `mid-fanout`, after `corner`: keep it if R12 rises by 25% and R1 does not rise.
records.rules: A minimum gap between routes, lane separation, wide crossing angles.
records.hardRules: project, then RULE-046.
records.zoom: anchor. The charge falls with the level, so far views keep their bundles.

records.name: Magnetic springs: a field that turns segments to a direction

sources.title: Graph drawing by the magnetic spring model

records.mechanism: A magnetic field turns each segment toward the nearest field direction. The field can be orthogonal, octilinear, radial from a hub or parallel to the main flow. The torque gives the drawing a style rule without a grid.
records.math: τ = k_m ‖s‖^α θ^β, θ = angle from the nearest field direction, two equal forces at the ends of s, at right angles to s
records.cost: O(I·V). 100 nodes: 5 ms. 1000 nodes: 60 ms.
params: field: orthogonal, octilinear, radial or flow
records.screen: On `grid-400` and `mid-uniform`, from `straight`: keep it if R14 reaches 0.8 or more with R6 up by 10% or less.
records.rules: Orthogonal or octilinear segments, a main flow direction, radial fans around hubs.
records.hardRules: project. The plug stubs keep SIDE_NORMAL.
records.zoom: The field is the same at each level, so the directions do not change between levels. anchor.

records.name: Harmonic potential field router

sources.title: Path planning using Laplace's equation
Real-time obstacle avoidance for manipulators and mobile robots

records.mechanism: The router solves the Laplace equation on a grid. The boxes hold the highest potential, and the target plug holds zero. The route follows the steepest descent. A harmonic function has no local minimum in the free space, so each descent reaches its target.
records.math: ∇²u = 0 in free cells, u = 1 on boxes, u = 0 at the target, solved by SOR or multigrid. Route: dx/dt = -∇u
records.cost: O(G) per target with multigrid, for G cells. 100 nodes: 0.4 s (one solve per target box). 1000 nodes: 30 s or more, so only the far levels or one solve per group.
records.screen: On `case-dense-groups` and `packedGridBoard`, 100 nodes: keep it if R9 = 0, R8 rises by 40% and R6 is 1.3 times `corner` or less.
records.rules: Clearance (the potential is high near boxes), smooth routes, routes that stay in the middle of gaps.
records.hardRules: guard. The descent does not enter a box cell, because the potential is at its maximum there. The end snaps to the plug.
records.zoom: The coarse grid of the parent level starts the solve, so the field changes little between levels.

records.name: Distance field and fast marching: the geodesic router

sources.title: A fast marching level set method for monotonically advancing fronts
Distance transforms of sampled functions

records.mechanism: A distance transform gives the signed distance φ to the nearest box. The speed falls near the boxes. Fast marching gives the travel time from the target, and the route descends it. The speed function writes clearance and area costs as one rule.
records.math: ‖∇T‖ = 1/F(x), F = clamp(φ/d0, ε, 1)^p, φ by the exact distance transform in O(G)
records.cost: O(G) for the transform, O(G log G) for each target. 100 nodes: 0.6 s. 1000 nodes: 30 s, so targets share one solve per group.
records.screen: Same boards as RULE-005, against `corner`: keep it if C7 and R8 rise by 30% at R6 of 1.2 times or less.
records.rules: Clearance, length, a cost for each area: dense regions, group interiors, margins.
records.hardRules: guard. F = 0 inside a box, so the time there is infinite.
records.zoom: warm. Each level uses its own level boxes and the coarse field of the parent.

records.name: Elastic rod: curvature forces on the curve

sources.title: Discrete elastic rods
sources.authors: Bergou, Wardetzky, Robinson, Audoly and Grinspun

sources.title: The curve of least energy

records.mechanism: The curve step treats a route as a discrete elastic rod. The bending energy is the sum of the squared turns over the local lengths. The descent lowers it while a projection keeps the clearance. The result has no sharp corner.
records.math: E_b = Σ_i (2 tan(θ_i/2))² / ℓ_i, ℓ_i = half the sum of the two neighbor segment lengths, plus a stretch term Σ (‖e‖ - ‖e0‖)²
records.cost: O(I·V). 100 nodes: 6 ms. 1000 nodes: 80 ms.
records.screen: On `shared-all` and `case-hub-chain`, after the curve `smooth`: keep it if C3 falls by 20% with 0 faults of C7.
records.rules: Smallest radius, small curvature change, no tangent break.
records.hardRules: project with φ ≥ clearance. The end tangents stay on SIDE_NORMAL.
records.zoom: anchor. The rod of the parent level is the start.

records.name: Stress majorization of the bend points

sources.title: Integrating edge routing into force-directed layout
Graph drawing by stress majorization

records.mechanism: Dwyer, Marriott and Wybrow put the bend points of the routes into a stress layout as extra nodes. Each bend point has a target distance to its neighbors and to the box corners that it wraps. Each step of stress majorization is one convex solve.
records.math: stress = Σ w_ij (‖x_i - x_j‖ - d_ij)², w_ij = d_ij^-2, each step solves L_w X = L_Z X0 by conjugate gradients
records.cost: O(I·V·k) with a sparse solve. 100 nodes: 30 ms. 1000 nodes: 600 ms.
records.screen: On `mid-clustered`, after `corner`: keep it if R6 and R4 fall by 10% and R1 does not rise.
records.rules: Target lengths, a distance to each wrapped corner, even spacing of the bends.
records.hardRules: project. Separation constraints keep each bend point on its side of each wrapped corner.
records.zoom: warm. Majorization descends from the start, so a warm start gives a near answer.

records.name: Separation constraints: the QP that nudges parallel segments

sources.title: IPSep-CoLa: an incremental procedure for separation constraint layout of graphs
WebCoLa: constraint-based layout in the browser
Orthogonal connector routing

records.mechanism: The router keeps the order of the parallel segments in a channel. A quadratic program then places them. It keeps each segment near the channel middle and each pair at least a gap apart. VPSC solves each axis. The fixed order makes the problem convex.
records.math: min Σ w_i (x_i - c_i)² subject to x_j - x_i ≥ g for each ordered pair, lo ≤ x_i ≤ hi. VPSC in O(s log s) for each axis
records.cost: O(s log s) for each channel of s segments. 100 nodes: 3 ms. 1000 nodes: 40 ms.
params: weight of the middle against the plug side 0 to 1
records.screen: On `mid-hubs` and `case-dense-groups`: keep it if each channel wide enough has each gap at `g` or more, with R1 unchanged.
records.rules: A gap between lanes, centered lanes, the bounds of a channel, alignment by equal constraints.
records.hardRules: Exact. The channel bounds are the box walls minus the clearance. A channel too narrow for its lanes keeps the base route.
records.zoom: convex. The same order gives a small move for a small change.

records.name: Kamada-Kawai on the skeleton of the hubs

sources.title: An algorithm for drawing general undirected graphs

records.mechanism: The highways form a small graph, with the hubs and the junctions as its nodes. Kamada-Kawai places the free junctions so that their distances match the path lengths of the box graph. The boxes stay fixed and push the junctions out by a barrier.
records.math: E = Σ_{i<j} ½ k_ij (‖p_i - p_j‖ - ℓ d_ij)², k_ij = K / d_ij², Newton steps on one node at a time, barrier -ln(φ(p_i))
records.cost: O(I·h²) for h hubs. 100 nodes: 1 ms. 1000 nodes: 30 ms.
records.screen: On `case-hub-chain` and `mid-hubs` with `sections`: keep it if B3 falls by 10% and Z7 does not rise.
records.rules: Junction spacing, balanced hubs, distances that follow the graph.
records.hardRules: barrier at each junction, then the routes go through the corner graph.
records.zoom: anchor. Each level places its own hubs near the hubs of its parent.

records.name: Moves that keep the topology (PrEd, ImPrEd)

sources.title: A force-directed algorithm that preserves edge-crossing properties
ImPrEd: an improved force-directed algorithm that prevents nodes from crossing edges
Topology preserving constrained graph layout

records.mechanism: PrEd and ImPrEd move the points with any forces, but they limit each move so that no point crosses a segment. A route then keeps its way around the boxes and its crossings. Any force rule becomes safe: no move adds a box crossing or a route crossing.
records.math: For each point and each of 8 direction sectors: max move = ½ · distance to the nearest segment in that sector. Move = force clipped to that bound
records.cost: O(I·V·k). 100 nodes: 15 ms. 1000 nodes: 250 ms.
records.screen: As a wrapper of RULE-001 and RULE-003: keep it if R9 and the new crossings are 0 in each run, at 2 times the time or less.
records.rules: Any force rule. The limit keeps the crossing count and the side of each box.
records.hardRules: guard by construction. A point does not cross a box edge at any time.
records.zoom: The warm start fixes the topology, so the order of the routes does not change between levels.

records.name: Cassowary: rules with strengths

sources.title: The Cassowary linear arithmetic constraint solving algorithm

records.mechanism: Cassowary solves linear equations and inequalities with strengths: required, strong, medium and weak. The router writes the coordinate of each leg as a variable. A stronger rule wins over all weaker rules together. A small edit solves again fast.
records.math: Simplex with a lexicographic objective over the strengths. Examples: x_leg ≥ box.right + gap (required), x_leg = x_other (strong), x_leg = mid (weak)
records.cost: O(c) for an incremental edit, O(c²) at worst for c constraints. 100 nodes: 10 ms. 1000 nodes: 300 ms.
records.screen: On `grid-400` and `mid-uniform`, orthogonal routes: keep it if the `required` rows give 0 hard faults and the aligned legs rise by 30%, with R6 unchanged.
records.rules: Alignment, equal spacing, order, a distance to a box, centered legs.
records.hardRules: The required constraints hold the hard rules for the leg coordinates.
records.zoom: Each level solves again from the basis of its parent, so a small edit gives a small change.

records.name: Integer program for orthogonal routing: the exact reference

sources.title: Orthogonal connector routing
Seeing around corners: fast orthogonal connector routing
CP-SAT solver of OR-Tools

records.mechanism: The orthogonal visibility graph holds the candidate segments. A multi-commodity flow program picks one path for each edge. The objective sums length, bends and crossings with weights. On small boards the solver proves the best answer, which MEAS2 needs.
records.math: min Σ_e Σ_a c_a y_ea + β Σ bends + γ Σ z, flow conservation for each edge, z ≥ y_ea + y_fb - 1 for each crossing pair of arcs
records.cost: NP-hard. Boards of 20 edges or fewer take seconds. Not for 1000 nodes.
records.screen: On 30 boards of 8 to 15 edges, in CI: keep it if it proves the optimum on 80% or more, in 10 s or less each.
records.rules: Any linear rule: length, bends, crossings, capacity, forbidden arcs.
records.hardRules: Exact. Only the free arcs exist.
records.zoom: A penalty Σ ‖y - y_parent‖ for a change from the parent level.

records.name: Minimum cost flow for the fewest bends

sources.title: On embedding a graph in the grid with the minimum number of bends

records.mechanism: For a fixed embedding, Tamassia gets the bends of an orthogonal drawing from a minimum cost flow. Each unit of flow is a turn of 90 degrees. The flow gives the fewest bends that the angles permit. For routes among boxes, the faces come from the fixed boxes and the route order.
records.math: Network: each vertex supplies 4, each inner face takes 2·deg(f) - 4, the outer face takes 2·deg(f) + 4. Each arc costs 1 for each bend
records.cost: O(n^1.75 √log n). 100 nodes: 10 ms. 1000 nodes: 400 ms, plus the planarization of the routes.
records.screen: On `grid-400`, after `corner`: keep it if R3 falls by 15% at the same topology.
records.rules: Fewest bends, fixed angles at the plugs, orthogonal segments.
records.hardRules: The embedding comes from a guarded route, so the shape keeps it.
records.zoom: The parent level fixes the embedding, so the shape is stable.

records.name: SAT and CP-SAT on a grid of cells

sources.title: A new FPGA detailed routing approach via search-based Boolean satisfiability
CP-SAT solver of OR-Tools

records.mechanism: Each pair of a grid cell and an edge has a Boolean variable. The clauses say that each edge forms one connected path, each cell holds at most c lanes, and a box cell holds none. A SAT or CP-SAT solver finds a legal set, then lowers length and bends.
records.math: x_ec ∈ {0,1}, Σ_e x_ec ≤ cap(c), a path cell has 2 neighbors on the path and an end cell has 1, connectivity by lazy cuts
records.cost: NP-hard. A grid of 100 by 100 cells with 20 edges solves in seconds.
records.screen: On tight boards (`packedGridBoard`, 16 boxes): keep it if it routes each edge where `corner` with room fails, in 10 s or less.
records.rules: Capacity, forbidden areas, parity, any Boolean rule.
records.hardRules: Exact.
records.zoom: The solution of the parent level gives the hints of the solver.

records.name: Octilinear highways by a mixed integer program

sources.title: Drawing and labeling high-quality metro maps by mixed-integer programming

records.mechanism: Nöllenburg and Wolff draw metro maps with a mixed integer program. Each edge takes one of eight directions, keeps its order at each station and has a minimum length. Bends cost. On the skeleton of the highways, the trunks become octilinear lines, as on a transit map.
records.math: A binary for each edge and each of 8 sectors, big-M relations between x_v - x_u and the sector, circular order constraints. Objective: bends + relative position + length
records.cost: MIP. A skeleton of 100 edges or fewer takes minutes.
records.screen: On the skeleton of `mid-hubs` (60 trunk edges or fewer), in CI: keep it if it solves in 60 s or less with R14 = 1 and B3 up by 10% or less.
records.rules: Octilinear trunks, the order of the trunks, a minimum length, few bends, the relative position of the hubs.
records.hardRules: The boxes are fixed vertices with clearance constraints. Planarity cuts enter lazily.
records.zoom: Each level adds a term for the relative position to its parent.

records.name: Layers of rules in priority order

sources.title: Survey of multi-objective optimization methods for engineering

records.mechanism: The rules sit in layers: the hard rules first, then each group of soft rules in priority order. Each layer optimizes its terms, then holds its value within a slack while the next layers run. The user orders the rules and gives no weights.
records.math: For k = 1..L: f_k* = min f_k(x) subject to f_j(x) ≤ (1 + ε_j) f_j* for each j < k, with the hard rules as layer 0
records.cost: L times the inner solver.
records.screen: With RULE-019 inside, on `mid-clustered`: keep it if the first measure stays within ε of its own optimum and the second beats the weighted sum.
records.rules: Any rule. The layers express priority, not a weight.
records.hardRules: Layer 0 holds the hard rules as constraints.
records.zoom: The same layers run at each level. An option puts the stability term of RULE-045 in the first soft layer.

records.name: Wave function collapse with tiles of routes

sources.title: WaveFunctionCollapse
WaveFunctionCollapse is constraint solving in the wild

records.mechanism: The board becomes a grid of tiles: empty, straight, corner, cross, merge and box. Adjacency rules tell which tiles can touch. The solver fixes the cell with the least entropy and spreads the rules. Routes and highways appear as a pattern of tiles that obeys the rules.
records.math: Arc consistency over the cells, each with a domain of tiles. Pick the cell of least entropy with a seeded random number generator. Backtrack on a contradiction
records.cost: O(G·T) for each spread, plus restarts. 100 nodes: 50 ms. 1000 nodes: 2 s.
records.screen: On `grid-400`: keep it if each edge connects in 3 restarts or fewer with R14 = 1.
records.rules: Local rules of adjacency: no tee next to a box, merges only on lanes, a style of tiles.
records.hardRules: Box cells and plug cells are fixed. A path check for each edge adds the global rule that each edge connects.
records.zoom: The coarse tiles constrain the fine tiles.

records.name: Energy as a sum of rule terms, by gradient descent

sources.title: Graph drawing via gradient descent, (GD)^2
sources.authors: Ahmed, De Luca, Devkota, Kobourov and Li

sources.title: Penrose: from mathematical notation to beautiful diagrams
sources.authors: Ye, Ni, Krieger, Ma'ayan, Wise, Aldrich, Sunshine and Crane

records.mechanism: Each rule becomes a smooth term: a crossing angle, a clearance or a length. The energy is the weighted sum. Gradient descent moves all route points at once. (GD)² showed this for node layouts. Here the variables are the route points, and the boxes are fixed.
records.math: E(x) = Σ_r w_r E_r(x), x ← x - η ∇E. Smooth forms: clearance softplus(d0 - φ)², crossing angle cos²θ, length Σ ‖x_{i+1} - x_i‖²
records.cost: O(I·(V + P)) for P pairs. 100 nodes: 50 ms. 1000 nodes: 1 s with a grid for the pairs.
records.screen: On `mid-clustered`: keep it if its front over R1, R6 and R8 has a point that `corner` with RULE-001 does not dominate.
records.rules: Any rule with a smooth form or a smooth substitute.
records.hardRules: barrier for the boxes, then RULE-046.
records.zoom: anchor and warm.

records.name: Adam with a seeded sample of pairs

sources.title: Adam: a method for stochastic optimization
Multicriteria scalable graph drawing via stochastic gradient descent, (SGD)^2
sources.authors: Ahmed, De Luca, Devkota, Kobourov and Li

sources.title: Graph drawing by stochastic gradient descent

records.mechanism: Pair terms of route against route cost O(V²). Adam with a seeded sample of pairs makes each step O(V). The step size falls on a schedule, as in the SGD layouts of stress. A fixed seed and a fixed order keep the result the same each time.
records.math: m ← β1 m + (1 - β1) g, v ← β2 v + (1 - β2) g², x ← x - η_t m̂ / (√v̂ + ε), η_t = η0 e^{-λt}, g from a seeded sample of pairs
records.cost: O(I·V·s) for s samples of each point. 100 nodes: 30 ms. 1000 nodes: 400 ms.
records.screen: Against RULE-019 at the same time: keep it if it reaches the energy of RULE-019 in a third of the time or less at 1000 nodes.
records.rules: The same rules as RULE-019.
records.hardRules: The same as RULE-019.
records.zoom: anchor.

records.name: Simulated annealing over candidate routes

sources.title: Drawing graphs nicely using simulated annealing

records.mechanism: Each edge gets k candidate routes from the base router: the shortest, a detour on each side and a route along each near highway. Annealing changes the choice of one edge at a time. It accepts a worse total with a probability that falls with the temperature.
records.math: P(accept) = exp(-ΔE / T), T_k = T0 α^k. ΔE is local: the crossings of one edge come from a grid of segments
records.cost: O(S·k_n) for S changes and k_n segments near an edge. 100 nodes: 100 ms. 1000 nodes: 2 s.
records.screen: On `mid-clustered` and `mid-hubs`: keep it if R1 falls by 15% against the first choice, at the same R6.
records.rules: Any rule, also discrete rules: crossing counts, highway membership, lane capacity.
records.hardRules: guard. Each candidate obeys the hard rules.
records.zoom: hysteresis. The start state is the choice of the parent level, and a change costs.

records.name: Position-based dynamics: one rule at a time (XPBD)

sources.title: Position based dynamics
XPBD: position-based simulation of compliant constrained dynamics

records.mechanism: Position-based dynamics treats each rule as a constraint. Gauss-Seidel moves the points onto one constraint at a time. XPBD gives each rule a compliance, so a soft rule gives way and a hard rule does not. Games use it because it is stable at any step size.
records.math: Δλ = (-C(x) - α̃ λ) / (∇C M⁻¹ ∇Cᵀ + α̃), Δx = M⁻¹ ∇Cᵀ Δλ, α̃ = α / Δt². Constraints: segment length, φ(x) ≥ d0 with α = 0, bend angle, lane gap
records.cost: O(I·C) for C constraints. 100 nodes: 10 ms. 1000 nodes: 150 ms.
params: a fixed order of the constraints
records.screen: On `mid-clustered` and `case-dense-groups`, against RULE-001: keep it if it gets the same R8 in half the time, with R9 = 0.
records.rules: Lengths, distances, angles, alignment: each local rule.
records.hardRules: Compliance 0 for the boxes, a final pass, then RULE-046. The plugs have infinite mass.
records.zoom: anchor as a soft constraint to the place at the parent level.

records.name: Barrier and continuous collision checks (IPC)

sources.title: Incremental potential contact: intersection- and inversion-free, large-deformation dynamics
sources.authors: Li, Ferguson, Schneider, Langlois, Zorin, Panozzo, Jiang and Kaufman

records.mechanism: Incremental potential contact adds a log barrier that goes to infinity when a route point nears a box. A continuous collision check limits each line search. So each step stays free of boxes, not only the last step.
records.math: b(d) = -(d - d̂)² ln(d / d̂) for d < d̂, else 0. Step ≤ 0.8 · the time of first contact from the collision check
records.cost: O(I·V·k) plus the collision checks. 100 nodes: 40 ms. 1000 nodes: 800 ms.
records.screen: With the energy of RULE-019 on `mid-clustered`: keep it if R9 = 0 at each step, at 2 times the time of RULE-019 or less.
records.rules: Clearance as a barrier, with any smooth energy.
records.hardRules: barrier. Each step is legal.
records.zoom: anchor.

records.name: Multigrid over the zoom levels

sources.title: A multigrid tutorial, second edition
A multilevel algorithm for force-directed graph-drawing
Efficient, high-quality force-directed graph drawing

records.mechanism: The zoom levels form a hierarchy of grids. The far level solves the rule energy on its few links first. Each finer level starts from the coarse answer and smooths it. A V-cycle sends the fine errors back up, so the levels agree.
records.math: Restriction R and prolongation P. V-cycle: ν1 smooth steps on the fine level, restrict the residual, solve the coarse level, x_f ← x_f + P e_c, ν2 smooth steps
records.cost: O(V) for each cycle. 100 nodes: 20 ms. 1000 nodes: 200 ms.
params: prolongation: linear or along the lanes
records.screen: On `nestedGridBoard` and `mid-clustered`: keep it if Z10 falls by 30% against levels solved alone, at the same energy.
records.rules: The same energy at each level.
records.hardRules: project at each level.
records.zoom: Native. The coarse-to-fine order gives agreement between levels.

records.name: Prices for rules that couple edges (dual ascent, ADMM)

sources.title: Distributed optimization and statistical learning via the alternating direction method of multipliers
sources.authors: Boyd, Parikh, Chu, Peleato and Eckstein

sources.title: PathFinder: a negotiation-based performance-driven router for FPGAs

records.mechanism: A hard rule that couples edges gets a price, for example the capacity of a gap. Each edge routes alone with the prices as costs. A price rises where its rule fails and falls where it holds. This is negotiated routing, written as dual ascent.
records.math: L = Σ_e c(P_e) + Σ_g λ_g (use_g - cap_g), λ_g ← max(0, λ_g + ρ (use_g - cap_g))
records.cost: O(K·m·A) for K rounds and the A* time A. 100 nodes: 200 ms. 1000 nodes: 5 s.
records.screen: On `case-dense-groups` and `packedGridBoard`: keep it if the lanes over capacity fall to 0 in 10 rounds or fewer, with R6 up by 10% or less.
records.rules: Capacity, crowding, each rule that couples edges.
records.hardRules: guard. The search of each edge uses the corner graph.
records.zoom: warm. The prices of the parent level start each level.

records.name: Motion planners: CHOMP and TrajOpt

sources.title: CHOMP: gradient optimization techniques for efficient motion planning
Motion planning with sequential convex optimization and convex collision checking
sources.authors: Schulman, Duan, Ho, Lee, Awwal, Bradlow, Pan, Patil, Goldberg and Abbeel

records.mechanism: Robot motion planners treat a path as one vector. CHOMP descends a smoothness term and an obstacle term with a gradient that spreads each update along the path. TrajOpt solves a series of convex programs with a hinge on the signed distance.
records.math: CHOMP: x ← x - η A⁻¹ ∇U, A = KᵀK the finite difference metric. TrajOpt: Σ max(0, d0 - sd(x_i)) inside a trust region
records.cost: CHOMP O(I·V) with a banded solve. 100 nodes: 30 ms. 1000 nodes: 500 ms.
records.screen: Against RULE-001 on the same boards: keep it if C3 is 20% lower at the same R8.
records.rules: Smoothness, clearance, length.
records.hardRules: The TrajOpt penalty rises until each point is legal, then RULE-046.
records.zoom: anchor.

records.name: Differentiable raster loss

sources.title: Differentiable vector graphics rasterization for editing and learning

records.mechanism: A differentiable rasterizer draws the routes into an image of R by R pixels. The losses read the image: ink over a cap, ink over boxes and gaps under a minimum width. Their gradients flow back to the route points. One pass costs the same for 10 edges or 10 000.
records.math: I(p) = Σ_s k(dist(p, s) / w), L = Σ_p max(0, I(p) - ρ_max)² + λ Σ_p I(p) M_box(p), gradients by DiffVG or a soft kernel
records.cost: O(R² + V·k). 100 nodes: 30 ms at 256². 1000 nodes: 80 ms.
records.screen: On `mid-clustered` and `large-clustered`: keep it if the peak density falls by 30% with R6 up by 10% or less.
records.rules: Density, clutter, ink over boxes, white space, any rule that reads an image.
records.hardRules: The box term is soft, so project and RULE-046.
records.zoom: Each level renders at its own scale, so each zoom gets its own loss.

records.name: Density bundling with a mask of the free space

sources.title: Graph bundling by kernel density estimation
CUBu: universal real-time bundling for large graphs
sources.authors: van der Zwan, Codreanu and Telea

records.mechanism: KDEEB moves each route point up the gradient of the density of all routes. Routes gather into ridges, and the ridges become highways. The rule version multiplies the density by a mask of the free space, so no ridge forms over a box.
records.math: ρ = K_h * Σ δ(x_i) by splat and blur, x_i ← x_i + η ∇ρ / ‖∇ρ‖, mask ρ · [φ > d0], then smooth along the route
records.cost: O(I·(R² + V)). 100 nodes: 40 ms. 1000 nodes: 150 ms.
records.screen: On `mid-clustered` against `shared`: keep it if B1 is equal or better with R9 = 0 after the projection.
records.rules: Ink, bundles, free space.
records.hardRules: project, then RULE-046.
records.zoom: The kernel width h grows with the level, so the ridges nest.

result.note: The strategy `kdeeb` beats `shared` on 0 of the 4 boards alone. With the gate `stretch`, it wins 1 (small-clustered). B1 rises on 3 boards, with a paired median ratio of 1.15. The density of the first routes (`kdeeb-routes`) wins 2 (small-clustered, dense-groups). Without the mask, the q95 rises to 1.06 to 1.26.

strict.note: With the strict rule, kdeeb-routes against shared wins 2 of 4 boards (2 with the old rule). The verdict does not change.

activation.note: 4 of 4 candidates are exercised on a decision board. The verdict does not change.

records.name: Clutter measure as a loss

sources.title: Measuring visual clutter
Differentiable vector graphics rasterization for editing and learning

records.mechanism: Feature congestion measures clutter from the local spread of color, direction and contrast. This rule takes the direction part: many route directions in one area show as clutter. The loss lowers that spread, so near routes turn parallel or cross at right angles.
records.math: T(p) = K * Σ_s w_s (cos 2θ_s, sin 2θ_s), clutter(p) = 1 - ‖T(p)‖ / Σ w_s, L = Σ_p clutter(p), gradients through the soft raster
records.cost: The same as RULE-027.
records.screen: On `mid-uniform` and `mid-clustered`: keep it if the clutter falls by 20% and R2 rises.
records.rules: Visual order, alignment to the flow, right-angle crossings.
records.hardRules: project, then RULE-046.
records.zoom: Each level has its own resolution.

records.name: Medial axis of the free space as the highway line

sources.title: Skeleton-based edge bundling for graph visualization
sources.authors: Ersoy, Hurter, Paulovich, Cantareiro and Telea

sources.title: Distance transforms of sampled functions

records.mechanism: The medial axis of the free space holds the points at equal distance from two boxes. It is the line of the most clearance. This rule pulls the trunks of the highways onto the axis and prunes its short branches. Skeleton bundling does the same with the density of the routes.
records.math: Skeleton from the ridges of the distance transform, pruned by branch length. Pull k ∇dist(x, axis) on the trunk points
records.cost: O(G) for the transform and the skeleton. 100 nodes: 20 ms. 1000 nodes: 100 ms.
records.screen: On `packedGridBoard` and `case-dense-groups`: keep it if the trunk R8 doubles with B3 up by 10% or less.
records.rules: Clearance, lanes in the middle of gaps, highways in the gaps.
records.hardRules: The axis is in the free space by definition.
records.zoom: The prune length grows with the level, so the skeletons nest.

records.name: One render loss summed over the zoom levels

sources.title: Differentiable vector graphics rasterization for editing and learning

records.mechanism: One route set serves each zoom level. This loss renders the drawing at the scale of each level and sums the image losses with weights. A route that reads well near and far wins. One trade replaces a separate tune for each level.
records.math: L = Σ_ℓ ω_ℓ L_img(render(x, s_ℓ)), with s_ℓ the scale of level ℓ and the line width fixed in screen pixels
records.cost: The number of levels times RULE-027. 100 nodes: 100 ms. 1000 nodes: 250 ms.
params: a weight ω for each level
records.screen: On `nestedGridBoard`: keep it if the worst level loss falls by 20% and Z10 is better than levels solved alone.
records.rules: Legibility at each zoom.
records.hardRules: project, then RULE-046.
records.zoom: Native. One geometry serves all levels.

records.name: Wavefront automaton with rule costs (Lee)

sources.title: An algorithm for path connections and its applications

records.mechanism: A cellular automaton spreads a wave from the source cell. Each cell takes the minimum of its neighbors plus a cost. The cost table holds the rules: a turn costs, a cell near a box costs, a cell on a highway costs less. The trace back gives the route.
records.math: T(c, d) = min over neighbors n of T(n, d') + w(c) + τ [d ≠ d'], state = cell and direction, buckets for small integer costs
records.cost: O(4G) for each edge. 100 nodes: 0.3 s. 1000 nodes: 5 s, so a corridor is necessary.
records.screen: On `grid-400`: keep it if R3 is equal to `corner` or lower, with R9 = 0, in 2 times the time or less.
records.rules: Bends, clearance, highway preference, forbidden cells, rules of direction.
records.hardRules: guard. A box cell does not enter the wave.
records.zoom: The route of the coarse grid limits the fine search to a corridor.

records.name: Sandpile automaton for the capacity of gaps

sources.title: Self-organized critical state of sandpile automaton models

records.mechanism: Each cell of a gap holds lanes like grains of sand. A cell over its capacity topples and sends one lane to each free neighbor. The abelian property makes the final state the same for each order of topples. So the spread of the lanes needs no seed.
records.math: If h(c) ≥ cap(c): h(c) -= deg(c), and h(n) += 1 for each free neighbor n. The stable state is unique (Dhar)
records.cost: O(G·t) for t topples. 100 nodes: 5 ms. 1000 nodes: 50 ms.
records.screen: On the gaps of `case-dense-groups`: keep it if each cell holds its capacity or less and R12 rises by 20%.
records.rules: Capacity of a gap, an even spread of crowded lanes.
records.hardRules: Box cells are walls, so no lane goes into a box. The routes then follow the cells that they get.
records.zoom: Each level has its own capacity. The state of the parent level adds as grains.

records.name: Shape grammar: rewrite rules on parts of routes

sources.title: Shape grammars and the generative specification of painting and sculpture

records.mechanism: A shape grammar holds rewrite rules on parts of routes. A jog of two short legs becomes one leg. A turn back becomes a detour around a corner. Two parallel routes become a lane pair. A rule applies only when its result obeys the hard rules.
records.math: Rules L → R with a guard g(R), applied in a fixed priority order to a fixed point. Critical pairs check that the order does not change the result
records.cost: O(V·r·p) for r rules and p passes. 100 nodes: 5 ms. 1000 nodes: 60 ms.
records.screen: On `mid-clustered` after `corner`: keep it if R3 plus R7 falls by 10% with 0 hard faults.
records.rules: Local style rules and simplifications.
records.hardRules: guard. Each rewrite checks its result.
records.zoom: A grammar for each level. The coarse levels use the merge rules more.

records.name: L-system trees for a fan-out

sources.title: The algorithmic beauty of plants

records.mechanism: An L-system grows a highway from a hub like a branch. Each step rewrites a trunk symbol into a trunk and branches, with angles and lengths from the rules. A branch stops at its targets or at a box. The grammar fixes the style of a fan-out.
records.math: T → F [+B] F [-B] T with angle δ and length factor r. An open L-system asks φ at each step and stops at a box
records.cost: O(b) for b branches. 100 nodes: 1 ms. 1000 nodes: 10 ms.
records.screen: On `mid-fanout`: keep it if B6 is in its target band with R6 up by 15% or less against `trunks`.
records.rules: Branch angles, branch spacing, symmetry.
records.hardRules: The query of the environment stops growth at a box. RULE-046 repairs the last legs.
records.zoom: Depth d of the derivation is level d, so the trees nest.

records.name: A rule language that compiles to energy and constraints

sources.title: Penrose: from mathematical notation to beautiful diagrams
sources.authors: Ye, Ni, Krieger, Ma'ayan, Wise, Aldrich, Sunshine and Crane

sources.title: SetCoLa: high-level constraints for graph layout
Bluefish: composing diagrams with declarative relations
sources.authors: Pollock, Mei, Huang, Evans, Jackson and Satyanarayan

records.mechanism: A user writes rules as data: a selector of routes, segments or boxes, and a term, for example a minimum gap or an equal angle. A compiler turns each rule into an energy term or a constraint. Penrose does this for diagrams. One solver then solves all rules.
records.math: Rule = {select, term, weight or hard}. E = Σ_r w_r Σ_{t ∈ sel_r} f_r(t). Hard rules go to the constraint solver (RULE-022 or RULE-023)
records.cost: The cost of the solver, plus O(t) to evaluate t terms.
records.screen: Write RULE-001, RULE-003 and RULE-049 as rule files: keep it if each compiled run matches the hand-written run within 1% on 3 boards.
records.rules: Each term of the library. A user adds rules without code.
records.hardRules: Hard rules compile to constraints, then RULE-046.
records.zoom: The rule set applies at each level. A rule can name a level.

records.name: Answer set programs for the discrete choices

sources.title: Multi-shot ASP solving with clingo

records.mechanism: Answer set programming writes discrete rules as logic. An edge joins a highway if its stretch stays under a budget. No gap holds more than c lanes. The clingo solver finds the stable models and lowers the weak constraints. The geometry comes after.
records.math: { on(E,H) : cand(E,H) } 1 :- edge(E).  :- cap(G,C), #count{E : use(E,G)} > C.  #minimize { W,E : cost(E,W) }.
records.cost: Exponential at worst. Small for 200 edges or fewer in practice.
records.screen: On `mid-hubs`: keep it if it finds the best membership in 5 s or less and B3 falls against the rule of `trunks`.
records.rules: Highway membership, capacity, exclusion, derived rules in the style of Datalog.
records.hardRules: Integrity constraints.
records.zoom: A rule says that each fine highway sits in its parent highway.

records.name: Rule weights from preferences

sources.title: Aesthetic discrimination of graph layouts
Rank analysis of incomplete block designs: I. The method of paired comparisons

records.mechanism: People pick the better drawing of each pair. A Bradley-Terry model fits the weights of the rule terms so that the energy ranks the drawings in the same order. The weights then drive the solver. The fit is offline, so the routes stay the same for each run.
records.math: P(a ≻ b) = σ(w · (m_b - m_a)), maximize the log likelihood with an L2 term. m = the vector of MEAS0 values
records.cost: A logistic fit, under 1 s. No cost at run time.
records.screen: 200 pairs from a panel on made-up boards: keep it if it agrees with 75% or more of the held-out pairs.
records.rules: The weights of any rule set.
records.hardRules: No change. The solver keeps them.
records.zoom: One weight vector for each level, from views of that level.

records.name: A frozen critic network as a loss

sources.title: Evaluating the readability of force directed graph layouts: a deep learning approach
sources.authors: Haleem, Wang, Puri, Wadhwa and Qu

sources.title: Aesthetic discrimination of graph layouts

records.mechanism: A small network learns to score drawings from images and pairs of preferences. Then its weights freeze. The critic becomes one term of the energy, and its gradient flows through the raster. A fixed network gives a fixed answer.
records.math: L = L_rules + λ (-critic(render(x))), a small CNN on images of 64² to 256², gradients through DiffVG
records.cost: 5 ms for each pass on the CPU at 128². 100 nodes: 300 ms. 1000 nodes: 400 ms.
records.screen: Keep it if the critic score rises and no MEAS0 measure gets worse by more than 5%.
records.rules: A learned taste.
records.hardRules: project, then RULE-046.
records.zoom: A render for each level.

records.name: A graph network that gives a warm start

sources.title: DeepGD: a deep learning framework for graph drawing using GNN
Graph neural networks for graph drawing

records.mechanism: A graph neural network reads the route points, the boxes and the links between them. It gives a move for each point in one pass. It trains on the rule energy as its loss, as DeepGD trains on stress. At run time it gives the warm start of an exact solver.
records.math: h_i' = φ(h_i, Σ_j ψ(h_i, h_j, e_ij)), output Δx_i, loss E_rules(x + Δx)
records.cost: O(L·E) for L layers. 100 nodes: 20 ms. 1000 nodes: 100 ms. Training in CI only.
records.screen: Keep it if it cuts the solver steps by 50% to reach the same energy on held-out fixtures.
records.rules: The rules of the training loss.
records.hardRules: RULE-046 after the pass.
records.zoom: A pass for each level, with the place at the parent level as a feature.

records.name: A neural time field (NTFields)

sources.title: NTFields: neural time fields for physics-informed robot motion planning

records.mechanism: NTFields trains a network to give the travel time between two points. The time solves the eikonal equation with a speed that falls near the obstacles. A route is the descent of the time. The network takes the place of a grid solve for each target.
records.math: ‖∇_x T(x_s, x)‖ = 1 / S(x), the loss is the residual of this equation, S from φ
records.cost: Training for each board takes seconds to minutes. Queries take 1 ms.
records.screen: Keep it if one field trained for a board routes 1000 edges faster than RULE-006 at the same R8.
records.rules: Clearance through the speed, length.
records.hardRules: RULE-046 after the descent.
records.zoom: One field for each level.

records.name: Reinforcement learning distilled into a fixed scorer

sources.title: A deep reinforcement learning approach for global routing
sources.authors: Liao, Zhang, Dong, Poczos, Shimada and Kara

sources.title: A graph placement methodology for fast chip design

records.mechanism: A policy learns to order the edges and to choose their candidates. Its reward is the rule energy at the end. A policy that samples gives a new answer each run. So the trained policy distills into a fixed score, and the router takes its best candidate in a fixed order.
records.math: Policy gradient with the reward -E, then a regression fit of the score s(e, cand), then the maximum with a fixed tie break
records.cost: Training is large, in CI only. Inference O(m·k). 1000 nodes: 50 ms.
records.screen: Keep it if the distilled score beats RULE-021 at the same time on 3 families.
records.rules: Each rule of the reward.

records.zoom: The state holds the choice of the parent level.

records.name: Imitation of the exact solver

sources.title: Orthogonal connector routing

records.mechanism: On small boards, the exact program of RULE-013 gives the best routes. A ranker learns which candidate the solver chose for each edge, from features, for example length, bends and crossings. The router then ranks the candidates on large boards.
records.math: Features f(e, cand), a linear or tree ranker with a pairwise loss, the best candidate of each edge in a fixed order
records.cost: Inference O(m·k). 1000 nodes: 50 ms.
records.screen: Keep it if the gap to the optimum on held-out small boards falls by 30% against the first candidate.
records.rules: The rules of the exact objective.

records.name: Corner graph with rule prices, then rip-up and reroute

sources.title: PathFinder: a negotiation-based performance-driven router for FPGAs
Orthogonal connector routing

records.mechanism: The corner graph of today prices each arc by its length. This router adds rule prices: a turn, an arc near a box, an arc on a used lane and an arc along a highway. A* routes each edge. Then the worst edges route again with the prices of the others.
records.math: c(a) = ℓ(a) (1 + α [near box] + β use(a) - γ [on highway]) + τ turn(a). Rounds: route all, rank by E_e, remove the top q%, route them again
records.cost: O(R·q·m·A) for R rounds. 100 nodes: 50 ms. 1000 nodes: 1.5 s.
records.screen: On `mid-clustered` and `case-dense-groups`, against `corner`: keep it if R1 and R3 fall by 10% with R6 up by 5% or less and 0 hard faults.
records.rules: Bends, clearance, crowding, highway preference, each rule on an arc.
records.hardRules: guard. Only free arcs exist. The plugs are fixed.
records.zoom: A discount on the arcs of the routes of the parent level.

records.name: Continuation anchor between the zoom levels

sources.title: A multigrid tutorial, second edition

records.mechanism: Each level solves its rules with one more term: the squared distance of each shared route point from its place at the parent level. The weight falls as the levels get finer. Routes then move little between levels. A convex energy gives a bounded move.
records.math: E_ℓ(x) = E_rules(x) + μ_ℓ Σ_i ‖x_i - P(x_{ℓ-1})_i‖², μ_ℓ = μ0 κ^ℓ. For an m-convex E: ‖x*_ℓ - P x*_{ℓ-1}‖ ≤ ‖∇E_rules(P x*_{ℓ-1})‖ / (μ_ℓ + m)
records.cost: No extra cost.
records.screen: On `nestedGridBoard` and `mid-clustered`: keep it if Z10 falls by 40% with the energy of each level up by 5% or less.
records.rules: Stability between levels.
records.hardRules: The same as the base solver.
records.zoom: Native.

records.name: One repair step for the hard rules after any method

sources.title: Distance transforms of sampled functions
Orthogonal connector routing

records.mechanism: Any soft method can leave a fault. This step repairs each route. It pushes points out of boxes along the distance gradient, snaps the ends to the plug side and tests each segment. A segment that still fails gets a corner graph detour. A route that still fails keeps its base route.
records.math: x ← x + max(0, d0 - φ(x)) ∇φ(x) for k passes. Exact segment-box test. Fallback: local A* between the last good points, then the base route
records.cost: O(V + f·A) for f faults. 100 nodes: 2 ms. 1000 nodes: 20 ms.
params: the fallback: detour or base route
records.screen: After each soft method: keep it if the hard faults are 0 on 9 fixtures with 5 seeds, and it changes 5% of the points or fewer.
records.rules: The hard rules no-pass-through, ends-at-plugs, link-ends and complete.
records.hardRules: Exact, because of the fallback to the base route.
records.zoom: It changes only the parts with a fault, so it adds little change between levels.

result.note: R9 is the sum of route.through by router over the 14 inputs. R1 is route.ink and R5 the median detour, by router on packed-grid. The hard breaks go to 0 for each router on each input, packed-grid too. On packed-grid the ink grows by 20% to 23% for most routers, 13% for sections, and drops 9% for sections-tree. A route without a fault keeps its points.

strict.note: The screen field of the record decides on the hard faults, not on the board count of B1 and the B3 q95. The hard counts stay exact. The repair takes R9 to 0 for each router on each input, so each router has fewer hard breaks. The verdict does not change.

rescreen.note: Z2 is 0 for each router, with and without the repair step, on each of the 14 inputs. Thus the repair is equal on Z2.

records.name: Pull toward the lane slots of the highway skeleton

sources.title: Force-directed edge bundling for graph visualization

records.mechanism: The highway step gives a skeleton of trunks. Each route point near a trunk gets a pull toward its nearest lane slot. The pull is one rule term, so the solver trades it against detour and clearance. An edge that does not fit stays off the trunk.
records.math: E_h = k Σ_i w(d_i) ‖x_i - slot_i‖², w(d) = max(0, 1 - d / r), slot = trunk point + lane offset
records.cost: O(V log T) for T trunk segments. 100 nodes: 3 ms. 1000 nodes: 30 ms.
records.screen: With the trunks of HWY-001 on `mid-clustered`: keep it if B2 rises by 15% with B3 up by 5% or less.
records.rules: Bundles with a lane order.
records.hardRules: project, then RULE-046.
records.zoom: One skeleton for each level. The skeletons nest.

records.name: A curriculum that adds the rules one at a time

sources.title: Graph drawing via gradient descent, (GD)^2
sources.authors: Ahmed, De Luca, Devkota, Kobourov and Li

records.mechanism: The solver starts with only the coarse rules: length and clearance from the boxes. It adds the fine rules one at a time: lane gaps, crossing angles and curvature. Each new rule starts from the last answer. This order avoids the poor local minima of the full energy from a raw start.
records.math: E_t = Σ_r s_r(t) w_r E_r, with s_r(t) going from 0 to 1 in stage r
records.cost: The same as the solver.
records.screen: On `mid-clustered` with 5 seeds: keep it if the final energy falls by 5% against the full energy at once, at the same number of steps.
records.rules: Any rule.
records.hardRules: The same as the solver.
records.zoom: The stages can follow the levels.

records.name: Torque to a right angle at each crossing

sources.title: Graph drawing via gradient descent, (GD)^2
sources.authors: Ahmed, De Luca, Devkota, Kobourov and Li

records.mechanism: At each crossing of two routes, a torque turns both segments toward a right angle. The torque acts only near the crossing, so the rest of each route keeps its shape. The rule makes crossings easy to read, without fewer crossings.
records.math: E = k cos²θ at a crossing of angle θ. The gradient goes to the four ends of the two segments and to a window of w points with a falloff
records.cost: O(X·w) for X crossings. 100 nodes: 2 ms. 1000 nodes: 30 ms.
records.screen: On `mid-uniform` and `mid-clustered`: keep it if the median R2 rises by 15 degrees with R6 up by 3% or less.
records.rules: Crossing angle.
records.hardRules: project, then RULE-046.
records.zoom: anchor.

records.name: Topology first, then one convex program for the geometry

sources.title: Edge routing with ordered bundles
Topology preserving constrained graph layout

records.mechanism: A discrete step fixes the way of each route around the boxes and the order of the routes in each channel. With those fixed, the free space of each segment is convex. One convex program then places all points. It has one answer, so it is the same each run and moves little for a small change.
records.math: Variables: the bend points. Linear constraints: the side of each wrapped corner, x_j - x_i ≥ g in each channel. Objective: Σ ‖x_{k+1} - x_k‖² + λ Σ ‖x_k - x_k0‖². Solved by ADMM
records.cost: O(I·V) by ADMM. 100 nodes: 20 ms. 1000 nodes: 300 ms.
records.screen: On `mid-clustered` and `case-dense-groups`, after `shared`: keep it if each channel with room has gaps of g or more and Z10 falls by 30%.
records.rules: Each convex quadratic rule: length, centered lanes, gaps, alignment.
records.hardRules: Exact. The constraints hold the hard rules.
records.zoom: convex. The same topology at each level gives a near geometry.

records.name: Streamlines of a summed current

sources.title: Path planning using Laplace's equation
Rules for biologically inspired adaptive network design
sources.authors: Tero, Takagi, Saigusa, Ito, Bebber, Fricker, Yumiki, Kobayashi and Nakagaki

records.mechanism: Each edge drives one unit of current from its source plug to its target plug through a sheet that conducts. The boxes insulate. The currents of the edges of one direction class add. Each route follows a streamline of its own current plus the total, so routes of one direction share channels.
records.math: ∇·(σ ∇u_e) = δ_s - δ_t for each edge, J = Σ σ ∇u_e for each direction class, the route traces J_e + β J by RK4
records.cost: One Poisson solve for each class, O(G) by multigrid. 100 nodes: 0.3 s. 1000 nodes: 3 s.
records.screen: On `mid-clustered`: keep it if B1 is equal to `shared` or better with R7 = 0.
records.rules: Bundles by flow, clearance (σ = 0 in boxes).
records.hardRules: No current enters an insulator, so the streamlines stay out of the boxes up to the error of the grid. Then RULE-046.
records.zoom: The coarse grid of the parent level starts the solve.

records.name: Rules that align and snap the legs

sources.title: The Cassowary linear arithmetic constraint solving algorithm
SetCoLa: high-level constraints for graph layout

records.mechanism: A reader sees aligned legs as one line. This rule finds legs of different routes with nearly equal coordinates and adds an equal constraint. It also snaps the leg coordinates to a grid of fixed pitch. A QP or XPBD pass meets them where the boxes permit.
records.math: Cluster the leg coordinates within ε by a sorted sweep. Constraints x_a = x_b (strong) and x = k · pitch (weak), solved by RULE-009 or RULE-022
records.cost: O(L log L) for L legs. 100 nodes: 2 ms. 1000 nodes: 20 ms.
records.screen: On `grid-400` and `mid-uniform`: keep it if the count of distinct leg coordinates falls by 30% with R12 unchanged.
records.rules: Alignment, a snap grid, equal spacing.
records.hardRules: The bounds of the solver hold the hard rules.
records.zoom: The pitch doubles at each coarser level, so the alignment nests.

records.name: A hysteresis gate for discrete choices

sources.title: Drawing graphs nicely using simulated annealing

records.mechanism: A discrete choice flips when its score margin changes sign. An example is the highway that an edge takes. This gate keeps the choice of the parent level unless the new choice wins by a margin h. A small change of the input then flips few routes.
records.math: Take c_new only if S(c_new) < S(c_parent) - h. The same test applies to an edit over time
records.cost: O(1) for each choice.
records.screen: On `nestedGridBoard` with one box moved by 1 u: keep it if the route flips fall by 50% with the energy up by h or less.
records.rules: Stability of discrete choices.
records.hardRules: No change.
records.zoom: Native.

records.name: Free plugs on a side
records.mechanism: The router does not fix a free plug before the search. The search starts from the whole free side at once, so the first leg goes straight to the first corner. The plug is the foot of that leg.
records.math: Multi-source A*. For each corner c in the strip in front of the free side S, a start link has the cost dist(c, S) + λ · angle(c - foot(c), normal), with foot(c) the projection of c on S, clamped to the inset.
records.cost: O(k) more start links for each end, with k corners in the strip. Near T_c: 30 ms at 100 nodes, 1 s at 1 000 nodes.
params: minGap between two plugs of a side: 4 to 16, default 8
records.screen: A scratch run of this note gives the first data: a pure slide of the plug straightens 9% to 13% of the bent ends. Keep the full form when the median of R3 drops by 15% or more on small-clustered and case-dense-groups, with the minimum of R11 at 0.5 or more.

result.note: The option `plugs: side` of the router `corners` is off by default. The median R3 falls 11% to 33% and R4 falls 11% to 31%, with 0 new hard breaks. The bar of 15% on small-clustered and dense-groups is not met. R10 is 0 against 0. The values of `bend` and `most` do not change the records.

strict.note: The screen field of the record decides on R3, R4 and R11 of the router corners, not on the board count of B1 and the B3 q95. The median R3 falls 11% to 33%, much more than its minimum effect. The verdict does not change.

rescreen.note: The gap closed uses only the 3 boards `tiny-uniform` of 10 nodes. It is a hint, not a verdict.

activation.note: 1 of 1 candidates are exercised on a decision board. The verdict does not change.

records.name: Plug justification

sources.title: An empirical distribution function for sampling with incomplete information
sources.authors: Ayer, Brunk, Ewing, Reid and Silverman

sources.title: Breaking paragraphs into lines

records.mechanism: Each plug of a side has an ideal place, where its route wants to leave. The plugs keep their order and a gap of at least s_min. The plugs move the least distance from their ideal places.
records.math: Minimize Σ (x_i - a_i)^2 with x_(i+1) - x_i ≥ s_min and lo ≤ x_i ≤ hi. Put y_i = x_i - i · s_min: the problem is isotonic regression of a_i - i · s_min. Pool adjacent violators solves it in O(k), then clamp to the side.
records.cost: O(k log k) for each side with the sort, O(m log m) in total. Less than 1 ms at 100 nodes and 5 ms at 1 000 nodes.
params: ideal place: the straight line to the other end, or the first leg of the route
weight of each plug: 1, or the count of its edges
records.screen: On grid-400 and small-clustered, the minimum of R11 must reach 1.0 on each side with room for its plugs. Drop it when R1 grows by more than 2%.

result.note: The option `plugGap: 6` of the router `corners` raises the R11 minimum on all 6 families, but R11 does not reach 1.0. R1 grows more than 2% on dense-groups, small-clustered and many-groups. The option stays in the code, off by default. The board grid-400 is not in screen-v1.

strict.note: The screen field of the record decides on R11 and R1 of the router corners, not on the board count of B1 and the B3 q95. R1 grows more than 2% on 3 boards, a loss above the minimum effect. The verdict does not change.

rescreen.note: The gap closed uses only the 3 boards `tiny-uniform` of 10 nodes. It is a hint, not a verdict.

activation.note: 1 of 1 candidates are exercised on a decision board. The verdict does not change.

records.name: Plug auction

sources.title: The auction algorithm: a distributed relaxation method for the assignment problem

records.mechanism: Each side has slots at an even spacing. Each end of an edge bids for the slots of its box. The auction gives each end one slot at the lowest total cost, and no two ends share a slot.
records.math: Assignment problem with c(end, slot) = w_a · angle(slot → other end, normal) + w_d · detour estimate + w_x · crossings of the straight stubs. The auction of Bertsekas with ε-scaling: a bidder raises the price of its best slot by best - second + ε.
records.cost: O(s · k · log(C / ε)) for each box with k ends and s slots. Less than 2 ms at 100 nodes and 20 ms at 1 000 nodes.
params: slots on each side: 2 to 16, or side / s_min
records.screen: On case-dense-groups and small-clustered, keep it when R1 drops by 5% or more and the minimum of R11 is 1.0, with the q95 of R5 up by less than 3%.

records.name: Side spill by capacity

sources.title: Register allocation and spilling via graph coloring

records.mechanism: A side holds at most cap plugs at the spacing s_min. When more ends face that side, the ends with the lowest cost to move spill to the next side. A register allocator spills values in the same way.
records.math: cap_s = floor(len_s / s_min) - 1. Sort the ends of a full side by the spill cost: the gain of angle to the next side, clockwise or counter-clockwise. Move the cheapest ends until the side fits. Do at most 4 passes around the box.
records.cost: O(k log k) for each box. Less than 1 ms at 100 and at 1 000 nodes.
params: spill to: the nearer side, or both sides
records.screen: On mid-fanout (in CI) and a case board with a fan of 20 edges, count the sides with R11 below 1. Keep it when that count drops to 0 and the mean of R10 rises by less than 10°.

records.name: Angular cohorts share a plug

sources.title: Ckmeans.1d.dp: optimal k-means clustering in one dimension by dynamic programming

records.mechanism: The ends of a box are sorted by the angle toward their other ends. Breaks in the angle split them into cohorts. Each cohort shares one plug and one short stub, then fans out.
records.math: Optimal 1D clustering of the angles by dynamic programming: minimize Σ variance within each cohort + β · cohorts. A cohort has 2 or more ends and a spread of θ_max or less.
records.cost: O(k^2) for each box with k ends. Less than 2 ms at 100 nodes and 20 ms at 1 000 nodes.
records.screen: On mid-fanout (in CI) and small-clustered, keep it when B1 rises by 0.05 or more and B4 rises by less than 0.02.

result.note: The strategy `stubs` beats `shared` on 1 of the 4 boards, and `ends: source` on 2. The q95 rises above 1 on hub-chain and many-groups, and B1 falls on hub-chain. B2 and R11 rise on all 4 boards. B2 rises 9% to 37% on 3 of them. B4 is worse on all 4 boards. R1 changes by 3% or less, but rises 29% on hub-chain.
